34-21-00-200-801IR Radial Position Error CheckPDF p. 287

6. IR Radial Position Error Check (Figure 201)

A. General

(1) This task provides the instructions to do a check of the inertial reference (IR) radial position error. (2) At the end of a flight, the radial position error of the IR can be calculated by comparing the IR final position to the airport position. The IR position data is available on the control display unit (CDU). NOTE: The IR radial position error calculation is not the same as the FMS calculation of IRS drift displayed on the IRS MONITOR page. NOTE: The Radial Position Error Check compares the IRS position to the LAT/LON position of the airplane while it is on the ground, and not moving. It is based on the length of time the ADIRU has been in NAV mode. This calculation is a more accurate representation of ADIRU IR drift than the FMS calculated value displayed on the IRS MONITOR page. (3) The IR radial position error limits are shown in a chart in this procedure.

B. References

Reference Title 34-21-01-000-801 Air Data Inertial Reference Unit Removal (P/B 401) 34-21-01-400-801 Air Data Inertial Reference Unit - Installation (P/B 401)

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-21-00-860-073 (1) Make sure the mode select switches on the mode select unit (MSU) are in the NAV position. NOTE: You must record the IR position data at the end of the flight while the IR stays in the NAV mode. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-001 (2) Do these steps to enter the airport identification into the CDU. (a) Push the RTE key on the CDU. 1) Make sure the RTE 1/1 shows on the CDU. (b) Put the airport identification into the CDU scratchpad. (c) Push the line select key (LSK) adjacent to the DESTon the CDU. 1) Make sure the airport identification shows below the DESTon the CDU. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-002 (3) Do these steps to enter the airplane present position into the CDU: NOTE: When the airplane is parked at an airport gate, the present position of the airplane is the gate latitude and longitude. (a) Put the gate latitude and longitude into the CDU scratchpad. NOTE: Do not use a space between the latitude and longitude. The format of the latitude and longitude data is as follows: Latitude and longitude: XDDMM.MYDDDMM.M Where: X is N or S for latitude 34-21-00 Y is E or W for longitude D is the number of degrees M is the number of minutes (b) Push the LEGS key on the CDU. 1) Make sure the LEGS 1/3 page shows on the CDU. (c) Push the LSK 1L on the CDU. 1) Make sure an identification waypoint of the gate latitude and longitude shows adjacent to the LSK 1L on the CDU. (d) Record the number in nautical miles that shows next to the first identification waypoint. NOTE: The first identification way point is the active waypoint that shows at the top of the LEGS 1/3 page. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-003 (4) Do these steps to transfer the left IRS position from the POS REF page to the LEGS page on the CDU: (a) Push the INIT/REF key on the CDU. 1) Make sure the INIT/REF INDEX page shows on the CDU. (b) Push the LSK adjacent to the <POS prompt on the CDU. 1) Make sure the POS INIT 1/3 page shows on the CDU. (c) Push the NEXT PAGE key on the CDU. 1) Make sure the POS REF 2/3 page shows on the CDU. (d) Push the LSK adjacent to the IRS L on the CDU. 1) Make sure the left IRS latitude and longitude data show on the CDU scratchpad. (e) Push the LEGS key on the CDU. 1) Make sure the LEGS 1/3 page shows on the CDU. (f) Push the LSK 2L on the CDU. 1) Make sure an identification waypoint of the IRS latitude and longitude shows adjacent to the LSK 2L on the CDU. (g) Record the number in nautical miles that shows next to the second identification waypoint. (h) Repeat these steps to record the number in nautical miles for the right IRS. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-004 (5) The difference between the gate and the IRS waypoints in nautical miles is the IR radial position error. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-005 (6) Compare the IR radial position error and the time the IRS was in the NAV mode to the radial position error limits (Figure 201). SUBTASK 34-21-00-020-001 (7) If one of these conditions occurs, replace the applicable ADIRU: (a) The IR radial position error is in the REPLACE-1 FLIGHT area. (b) The IR radial position error is in the REPLACE-2 CONSECUTIVE FLIGHTS area for the second consecutive flight. (c) These are the tasks: 34-21-00 Air Data Inertial Reference Unit Removal, TASK 34-21-01-000-801 Air Data Inertial Reference Unit - Installation, TASK 34-21-01-400-801

34-21-00-200-802Inertial Reference Residual Groundspeed Error CheckPDF p. 291

7. Inertial Reference Residual Groundspeed Error Check

A. General

(1) This task provides the instructions to do a check of the inertial reference (IR) residual groundspeed error. NOTE: The residual ground speed error check at the end of a flight is valid if a full alignment, or a fast realignment, was performed at the beginning of the flight, to reset the ADIRU's residual ground speed. (2) Groundspeed readout must be taken before the airplane has been stationary for three minutes. The system may zero the display after three minutes. NOTE: The residual ground speed must be taken right after the airplane comes to rest. Otherwise it may continue to change, influenced by the inertial system’s drift, and not be an accurate depiction of the residual ground speed after a flight leg. (3) The display of groundspeed may be blank after three minutes. NOTE: The residual ground speed is also displayed on the Flight Management System (FMS) Control Display Unit (CDU) POS REF page 2/3.

B. References

Reference Title 34-21-01-000-801 Air Data Inertial Reference Unit Removal (P/B 401) 34-21-01-400-801 Air Data Inertial Reference Unit - Installation (P/B 401)

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-21-00-860-075 (1) Set the SYS switch to the L position on the ISDU. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-006 (2) Set the DSPL switch to the TRK/GS position on the ISDU. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-007 (3) When the airplane is stationary, the ISDU display shows the residual groundspeed error. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-008 (4) Make sure these conditions do not occur: (a) The residual groundspeed error is 15 knots or larger after each of two consecutive flights, one after the other. (b) The residual groundspeed error is 21 knots or larger at the end of one flight. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-009 (5) If one of these conditions occurs replace the ADIRU. These are the tasks: Air Data Inertial Reference Unit Removal, TASK 34-21-01-000-801, Air Data Inertial Reference Unit - Installation, TASK 34-21-01-400-801. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-010 (6) Set the SYS switch to the R position. SUBTASK 34-21-00-200-011 (7) Do the procedure again for the right ADIRU.

(e) For seconds 2-10, make sure that: 1) The display segments and indicators on the ISDU are blank. 2) The FAULT , ON DC, and DC FAIL annunciators on the left side of the MSU go off. 3) The MASTER CAUTION and IRS lights on the captain's glareshield go off. 4) The HDG flag comes into view and the compass card goes out of view on the captain's Navigation Display (ND) and Primary Flight Display (PFD). 5) The HDG flag on the Standby Radio Magnetic Indicator (RMI) comes into view. 6) The ATT flag on the captain's PFD comes into view. 7) The VERT flag on the captain's PFD comes into view. (f) For seconds 10 and on, make sure that: 34-21-00 1) The 5° pitch up shows on the captain's PFD. 2) The 45° roll right shows on the captain's PFD. 3) The 15° heading shows on the captain's PFD and ND. 4) The 15° heading shows on the RMI. 5) The -10° slip/skid indicator angle shows on the captain's PFD. NOTE: The slip/skid indicator shows below the bank pointer on the PFD. 6) The vertical speed of -600 feet/minute descending (down pitch) shows on the captain's PFD. (g) Set the IRS switch on the P5 overhead panel to BOTH ON R. 1) Make sure that “---” shows in the HDG field on the ND or actual heading is shown if the system is fully aligned. (h) Release the DSPL SEL switch. (i) Set the IRS Transfer switch on the P5 overhead panel to the NORMAL position. SUBTASK 34-21-00-710-007 (2) Do these steps to do the self-test of the right IR system: (a) Set the SYS DSPL switch on the ISDU to the R position. (b) Set and hold the DSPL SEL switch on the ISDU in the TEST position. NOTE: The DSPL SEL switch is spring-loaded in the TEST position. It will return to the TK/GS position when released. Release the switch to stop the test. You will possibly have to do this step again to see all results of the test. (c) For seconds 0-2, make sure that: 1) The display segments and indicators on the ISDU come on. 2) The ALIGN, FAULT , ON DC, and DC FAIL annunciators on the right side of the MSU come on. 3) The MASTER CAUTION light on the first officer's glareshield comes on. SUBTASK 34-21-00-710-008 (1) Do these steps to do the self-test of the left ADR system: (a) Push the MACH AIRSPEED WARNING TEST NO. 1 switch on the P5 aft overhead panel for a moment. 1) Make sure that the overspeed warning clacker comes on momentarily. (b) Push the MACH AIRSPEED WARNING TEST NO. 2 switch on the P5 aft overhead panel for a moment. 1) Make sure that the overspeed warning clacker comes on momentarily. (c) Set the left mode select switch on the MSU to the ALIGN position. (d) Set the left altimeter baro correction data to 29.92 in/Hg (101.32 kPa). (e) Set the SYS DSPL switch on the ISDU to the L position. (f) Set and hold the DSPL SEL switch on the ISDU in the TEST position. (g) For the 0-2 seconds, make sure that the overspeed warning clacker comes on for 2 seconds. (h) After 7 seconds, make sure that: 1) The altitude of 10,000 ±40 ft (3048 ±12 m) shows on the captain's PFD. 2) The true airspeed of 170 ±4 knots (196 ±5 mph) shows on the captain's ND. 3) Total air temperature of 95 ±4°F (35 ±2°C) shows on the engine display. (i) Release the DSPL SEL switch. SUBTASK 34-21-00-710-009 (2) Do these steps to do the self-test of the right ADR system: (a) Push the MACH AIRSPEED WARNING TEST NO. 1 switch on the P5 aft overhead panel for a moment. 1) Make sure that the overspeed warning clacker comes on momentarily. (c) Set the right mode select switch on the MSU to the ALIGN position. (d) Set the right altimeter baro correction data to 29.92 in/Hg (101.32 kPa). (e) Set the SYS DSPL switch on the ISDU to the R position. (f) Set and hold the DSPL SEL switch on the ISDU in the TEST position. (g) For the 0-2 seconds, make sure that the overspeed warning clacker comes on for 2 seconds. (i) Release the DSPL SEL switch. F . Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition SUBTASK 34-21-00-860-098 (1) Set the mode select switches on the MSU to the OFF position. SUBTASK 34-21-00-860-045 (1) Do these steps to do a ISDU/FMC Digital and MCU Discrete Interface Test: (a) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name 006, 007, 018-020, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-506; 013, 014 PRE SB 737-34-2379; 043, 044 PRE SB 737-23-1484 D 15 C01050 FMCS CDU 2 507-999; 013, 014 POST SB 737-34-2379; 043, 044 POST SB 737-23-1484 D 15 C01239 FMCS MCDU 2 ALL (b) Set the left and right mode select switches on the MSU to the NAV position. (c) Set the SYS DSPL switch on the ISDU to the PPOS position. 1) Make sure the left and right ALIGN lights on the MSU are on. (d) Set the SYS DSPL switch on the ISDU to the L position. (e) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU 1. 1) Make sure the PERF INIT page shows on the CDU 1. (f) Push the LSK 6L adjacent to the <INDEX prompt on the CDU. 1) Make sure the INIT/REF INDEX page shows on the CDU 1. (g) Push the LSK 2L adjacent to the <POS prompt on the CDU. 1) Make sure the POS INIT 1/3 page shows on the CDU 1. (h) Enter the latitude of N0000.0 and the longitude of E00000.0 on the CDU 1. 1) Make sure the latitude and longitude show on the scratch pad of the CDU 1. NOTE: This may take up to 10 minutes. 3) Make sure the ENTER IRS POSITION shows on the CDU 1. 4) Make sure the latitude of N00°00.0' and the longitude of E000°00.0' show on the ISDU. 34-21-00 (j) Set the SYS DSPL on the ISDU to the R position. 1) Make sure the latitude of N00°00.0' and the longitude of E000°00.0' show on the ISDU. (k) Set the SYS DSPL on the ISDU to the L position. (l) Re-enter the latitude of N0000.0 and the longitude of E00000.0 on the CDU 1. 1) Make sure the latitude and longitude show on the scratch pad of the CDU 1. (m) Push the LSK 4R adjacent to the POS> prompt on the CDU. 1) Make sure the latitude and longitude show on the line 9 of the CDU 1. 2) Make sure the left and right ALIGN lights on the MSU come on steadily. 3) Make sure the left and right ALIGN lights start to flash when the alignment time reaches zero on the ISDU. (n) Enter the incorrect latitude of N00°00.0' on the ISDU. (o) Push the ENT key on the ISDU to send the latitude data. (p) Enter the correct longitude on the ISDU. NOTE: The correct longitude is dependent on the location of the airplane. (q) Push the ENT key on the ISDU to send the longitude data. 1) Make sure the left and right ALIGN and FAULT lights come on. 2) Make sure the MASTER CAUTION and the IRS lights on the glareshield come on. (r) Enter the correct latitude on the ISDU. NOTE: The correct latitude is dependent on the location of the airplane. (s) Push the ENT key on the ISDU to send the latitude data. (t) Enter the correct longitude on the ISDU. NOTE: The correct longitude is dependent on the location of the airplane. (u) Push the ENT key on the ISDU to send the longitude data. 1) Make sure the left and right FAULT lights go off. (v) Push the MASTER CAUTION switch on the glareshield to turn off the MASTER CAUTION and the IRS lights. (w) Set the DSPL SEL switch to the HDG/STS position. 1) Make sure there is no fault code shown on the ISDU. 2) Make sure the left ALIGN light on the MSU comes on steadily or goes off. 3) Make sure the aircraft true heading shows on the ISDU when the ALIGN light on the MSU went off. (x) Set the SYS DSPL switch on the ISDU to the R position. 1) Make sure there is no fault code shown on the ISDU. 2) Make sure the right ALIGN light on the MSU comes on steadily or goes off. 3) Make sure the aircraft true heading shows on the ISDU when the ALIGN light on the MSU went off. 34-21-00

G. Prepare for the Air Data Reference System Test

SUBTASK 34-21-00-860-079 WARNING KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES. THE AILERONS, ELEVATORS, RUDDER, FLAPS, SLATS, SPOILERS, STABILIZER AND NOSE GEAR CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-2 Row Col Number Name A 6 C00566 FLIGHT CONTROL FLAP LOAD RELIEF SUBTASK 34-21-00-860-085 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE EXTERNAL POWER TO DO THE TEST . IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THE APU WILL NOT SUPPLY SUFFICIENT POWER AND FAULT MESSAGES WILL SHOW. (2) Do this task: Supply External Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-813. SUBTASK 34-21-00-730-004 CAUTION OBEY THESE PRECAUTIONS BEFORE YOU APPLY PRESSURE TO THE PITOT- STATIC SYSTEM. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THESE PRECAUTIONS, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT AND INSTRUMENTS CAN OCCUR. (3) Obey these precautions before you apply pressure to the pitot-static system. (a) Make sure that the Air Data Inertial Reference System (ADIRS) has power when you install or remove the air data model test set, COM-1914. NOTE: This is to prevent possible incorrect pressure indications, unwanted fault messages, and system activations. (b) Pressure changes must be flow controlled to prevent sudden changes in pressure and possible damage to the air data hardware. 34-21-00 (c) Keep the static pressure in the range of 3.26 in/Hg (11.04 kPa) to 33.31 in/Hg (112.80 kPa). (d) Do not permit the static pressure to be more than 28 in/Hg (95 kPa) from the ambient pressure. (e) Keep the total pressure in the range of 3.26 in/Hg (11.04 kPa) to 41.34 in/Hg (139.99 kPa). (f) When you adjust the pressure, make sure that the rate of change of altitude is less than 5,000 feet per minute. (g) When you adjust the pressure, make sure that the rate of change of airspeed is less than 300 knots per minute. (h) Keep the static line pressure less than the pitot line pressure. (i) Make sure that the difference between the static and pitot line pressure is not larger than 10 in/Hg (34 kPa). (j) Make sure that the autopilot system stays off during the test. CAUTION MAKE SURE YOU DO NOT SUPPLY ELECTRICAL POWER TO THE PITOT PROBE HEATER. IF YOU DO, YOU CAN DAMAGE THE PITOT PROBE. (k) Make sure that the pitot probe heaters stay off during the test. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE AOA HEAT IS NOT ON. IF YOU DO NOT , INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (l) Make sure that the AOA probe heaters stay off during the test. (m) Connect the captain's, First Officer (F/O)'s, and alternate static systems together during the test. (n) Apply static pressure to all systems at the same time. (o) Connect the captain's, F/O's, and alternate pitot tubes together during the test. (p) Apply pitot pressure to all systems at the same time. SUBTASK 34-21-00-860-114 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE ATC TRANSPONDERS ARE IN THE STANDBY MODE WHEN YOU SIMULATE ALTITUDE. YOU CAN ACCIDENTALLY CAUSE TCAS TARGETS. AIR TRAFFIC IN THE AREA WILL CHANGE DIRECTION QUICKLY TO GO AWAY FROM THESE TARGETS. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (4) Make sure that the Air Traffic Control (ATC) transponders are in standby mode. (a) Set the Mode Select switch on the ATC control panel, P8, to STBY . 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-197

H. ADM and Standby Altimeter/Airspeed Indicator Test

SUBTASK 34-21-00-730-007 (1) Do these steps to do an ADM and Standby Altimeter/Airspeed Indicator Test: 34-21-00 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-197 (Continued) (a) Disconnect and plug the static pressure line at the cabin differential pressure indicator. (b) Turn the altimeter BARO knobs on the captain's Electronic Flight Instrument System (EFIS) control panel, F/O's EFIS control panel, and standby altimeter through the full range. (c) Set the altimeter BARO knobs on the captain's EFIS control panel, F/O's EFIS control panel, and standby altimeter to 29.92 in/Hg (101.32 kPa). 34-21-01-000-801Air Data Inertial Reference Unit RemovalPDF p. 329

2. Air Data Inertial Reference Unit Removal (Figure 401) CAUTION DUE TO THE CRITICAL ALIGNMENT OF THE AIR-DATA INERTIAL-REFERENCE UNITS, DISTURBANCE OR REMOVAL OF THE E5-2 SHELF REQUIRES RE- ALIGNMENT . THIS CAN ONLY BE ACCOMPLISHED BY AOG PERSONNEL USING SPECIALIZED ALIGNMENT TOOLING. CONTACT BEFORE DISTURBING THE MOUNTING SHELVES.

A. General

(1) This procedure gives instructions to remove the air data inertial reference unit (ADIRU). (2) The removal instructions are the same for the two ADIRUs.

B. References

Reference Title 06-41-00-800-801 Finding an Access Door or Panel on the Lower Half of the Fuselage (P/B 201) 20-10-07-000-801 E/E Box Removal (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right

D. Access Panels

Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

E. Removal Procedure

SUBTASK 34-21-01-860-001 (1) Set the applicable mode select switch on the IRS mode select unit (MSU) to the OFF position for at least 30 seconds. 34-21-01 SUBTASK 34-21-01-860-002 (2) For the left ADIRU, open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name E 5 C01009 ADIRU LEFT DC E 7 C01007 ADIRU LEFT AC CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name E 8 C00425 ADIRU LEFT EXC SUBTASK 34-21-01-860-011 (3) For the right ADIRU, open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name C 14 C01008 ADIRU RIGHT AC C 15 C00426 ADIRU RIGHT EXC C 17 C01010 ADIRU RIGHT DC SUBTASK 34-21-01-010-001 (4) To get access to the main equipment center, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door (TASK 06-41-00-800-801). SUBTASK 34-21-01-020-001 WARNING DO NOT REMOVE THE SHIMS FROM THE SHELF . SPECIAL EQUIPMENT AND AID IS NECESSARY TO ALIGN THE SHELF IF YOU REMOVE THE SHIMS. YOU CANNOT ALIGN THE SHELF IF YOU REMOVE THE SHIMS. IF YOU REMOVE THE SHIMS, THE AIR DATA WILL NOT BE ACCURATE, WHICH CAN CAUSE PROBLEMS WITH SAFETY OF FLIGHT . CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE CONNECTOR PINS OR OTHER CONDUCTORS ON THE ADIRU. IF YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ADIRU. CAUTION REMOVAL OF THE ADIRU WILL DISABLE THE GROUND CREW CALL FUNCTION OF THE EQUIPMENT COOLING LOW FLOW DETECTION. THIS COOLING LOW FLOW CONDITION COULD CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT . (5) Remove the ADIRU [1] from the shelf (TASK 20-10-07-000-801).

SUBTASK 34-21-02-860-004 (3) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name E 5 C01009 ADIRU LEFT DC E 7 C01007 ADIRU LEFT AC CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name E 8 C00425 ADIRU LEFT EXC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name C 14 C01008 ADIRU RIGHT AC C 15 C00426 ADIRU RIGHT EXC C 17 C01010 ADIRU RIGHT DC F . SUBTASK 34-21-02-860-006 (2) Set the two mode select switches on the IRS MSU to the NAV position. SUBTASK 34-21-02-710-001 (3) Do a test of the ISDU as follows: (a) Set the SYS DSPL switch on the ISDU [1] to the L position. (b) Hold the DSPL SEL switch on the ISDU [1] in the TEST position. (c) Make sure all the annunciators on the left side of the IRS MSU come on for approximately two seconds. (d) Release the DSPL SEL switch. (e) Set the SYS DSPL switch on the ISDU [1] to the R position. 34-21-02 (f) Hold the DSPL SEL switch on the ISDU [1] in the TEST position. (g) Make sure all the annunciators on the right side of the IRS MSU come on for approximately two seconds. (h) Release the DSPL SEL switch.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

C. Replacement of a Numeric/Alphanumeric Readout Lamp or a Decimal/Degree/Minute Lamp

SUBTASK 34-21-02-980-003 (1) Set the two mode select switches on the inertial reference system (IRS) mode select unit (MSU) to the OFF position. SUBTASK 34-21-02-860-009 (2) Open these circuit breakers and attach DO-NOT-CLOSE tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name E 5 C01009 ADIRU LEFT DC E 7 C01007 ADIRU LEFT AC CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name E 8 C00425 ADIRU LEFT EXC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name C 14 C01008 ADIRU RIGHT AC C 15 C00426 ADIRU RIGHT EXC C 17 C01010 ADIRU RIGHT DC SUBTASK 34-21-02-010-001 (3) Remove the transparent window filter assembly: 34-21-02 (a) Loosen the two captive screws that hold the window assembly to the ISDU. NOTE: Make sure that the lamps, spacers, or readouts do not fall into the ISDU. SUBTASK 34-21-02-960-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT PUT TOO MUCH PRESSURE ON THE LAMP WHEN YOU USE TWEEZERS. THE LAMP COULD BREAK AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (4) Replace the decimal/degree/minute lamp: (a) Hold the lamp at the bottom with the removal tool and pull straight out to remove it. (b) Remove and keep the spacer from the lamp. (c) Make sure that the wires on the new lamp are straight. (d) Install the spacer. (e) Carefully install the lamp. SUBTASK 34-21-02-960-002 (5) Replace the numeric/alphanumeric readout lamp: (a) Hold the perimeter of the readout lamp with the removal tool and pull straight out to remove it. (b) Push the new readout lamp into its position. 1) Make sure that the dimple indicator on the lamp is in the top left corner. SUBTASK 34-21-02-410-001 (6) Install the transparent window filter assembly: (a) Tighten the two captive screws that hold the window assembly to the ISDU. SUBTASK 34-21-02-860-010 (7) Remove the DO-NOT-CLOSE tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name E 5 C01009 ADIRU LEFT DC E 7 C01007 ADIRU LEFT AC CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name E 8 C00425 ADIRU LEFT EXC F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name C 14 C01008 ADIRU RIGHT AC C 15 C00426 ADIRU RIGHT EXC C 17 C01010 ADIRU RIGHT DC

D. Replacement test

SUBTASK 34-21-02-760-001 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 34-21-02-980-001 (2) Set the two mode select switches on the IRS MSU to the NAV position. 34-21-02 SUBTASK 34-21-02-710-002 (3) Do a test of the ISDU as follows: (a) Set the SYS DSPL switch on the ISDU to the L position. (b) Hold the DSPL SEL switch on the ISDU in the TEST position. (c) Make sure that all the annunciators on the left side of the IRS MSU come ON for approximately two seconds. (d) Release the DSPL SEL switch. (e) Set the SYS DSPL switch on the ISDU to the R position. (f) Hold the DSPL SEL switch on the ISDU in the TEST position. (g) Make sure that all the annunciators on the right side of the IRS MSU come ON for approximately two seconds. (h) Release the DSPL SEL switch.

E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 34-21-02-940-002 (1) Set the two mode select switches on the IRS MSU to the OFF position. SUBTASK 34-21-02-940-003 (2) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

G. Angle of Attack Sensor Installation

SUBTASK 34-21-05-860-002 (1) For the left AOA sensor, make sure that these circuit breakers are open: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name E 6 C01205 SMYD-1 SNSR EXC AC E 8 C00425 ADIRU LEFT EXC CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name C 3 C01072 HEATERS ALPHA VANE LEFT (2) For the right AOA sensor, make sure that these circuit breakers are open: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name D 3 C01071 HEATERS ALPHA VANE RIGHT 34-21-05 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name B 4 C01207 SMYD-2 SNSR EXC AC C 15 C00426 ADIRU RIGHT EXC SUBTASK 34-21-05-110-001 (3) To clean the surface around the AOA hole and surface of the alignment pins, do this task: Clean Bare, Clad, or Plated Metal with Solvent, TASK 20-10-34-110-802. SUBTASK 34-21-05-390-001 (4) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00633, to the alignment pins on the AOA sensor [1]. SUBTASK 34-21-05-420-001 (5) Do these steps to install the AOA sensor [1]: (a) Put the new gasket [4] into its position on the AOA sensor [1]. NOTE: It is not necessary to fit a new gasket if acquiring one will cause a flight delay. The old gasket, if in good condition, can be reused and replaced with a new gasket in one week or less. (b) Remove the protective caps from the electrical connectors [5]. (c) Examine the electrical connectors [5] for loose, bent, or broken pins. (d) Connect the electrical connectors [5] to the AOA sensor [1]. (e) Carefully put the AOA sensor [1] into position. (f) Install the screws [2] that hold the AOA sensor [1] to the airplane. (g) Tighten the screws [2] to 32 in-lb (3.6 N·m) - 39 in-lb (4.4 N·m). (h) Make sure that the face of the AOA sensor [1] aligns to within 0.04 in. (1.02 mm) or less of the airplane skin. NOTE: The surface of the sensor base must be flush with the skin surface within +/-0.04 in. (1.02 mm) at the forward and aft edges, upper and lower edge flushness not required. (i) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the base of the AOA sensor [1] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is less than 0.010 ohm (10 miliohm). (j) If the electrical bonding resistance is more than 0.010 ohm (10 miliohm), do these steps: 1) Remove the AOA sensor [1]. 2) Clean the bonding surfaces, including the countersunk holes in the AOA sensor [1] (SWPM 20-20-00). 3) Replace the screws with new screws. 4) Re-install the AOA sensor [1]. 5) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the base of the AOA sensor [1] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). a) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is less than 0.010 ohm (10 miliohm). 34-21-05 6) If the resistance is more than 0.010 ohms (10 miliohm), do these steps: a) Remove the AOA sensor [1]. b) Replace the nutplates and rivets that attach the AOA sensor [1] (SRM 51-40-02). c) Re-install the AOA sensor [1]. d) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the base of the AOA sensor [1] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). <1> Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. <2> Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is less than 0.010 ohm (10 miliohm). (k) Apply sealant, A00247, around the AOA sensor [1]. NOTE: It is not necessary to apply the sealant immediately, if the cure time will cause a flight delay. But, you must apply the sealant as soon as possible to keep the moisture out of the area between the probe and airplane skin. The sealant deferral must not exceed a maximum of eight weeks. NOTE: When sealant has reach the tack-free time, the airplane can be dispatched for flight. T ack-free time is when the sealant has properly adhered and capable of providing maximum protection to a surface. SUBTASK 34-21-05-860-041 (6) For the left AOA sensor, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name E 6 C01205 SMYD-1 SNSR EXC AC E 8 C00425 ADIRU LEFT EXC SUBTASK 34-21-05-860-042 (7) For the right AOA sensor, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name B 4 C01207 SMYD-2 SNSR EXC AC C 15 C00426 ADIRU RIGHT EXC SUBTASK 34-21-05-730-003 (8) Do this task: Angle of Attack System Test, TASK 34-21-05-730-801.

34-21-05-730-801Angle of Attack System TestPDF p. 369

2. Angle of Attack System Test (Figure 501)

A. General

(1) This task contains the Angle of Attack (AOA) sensor system test (also known as, Alpha Vane). NOTE: The AOA sensor is required to be tested through both the Air Data Inertial Reference Unit (ADIRU) and the Stall Management Yaw Damper (SMYD). NOTE: When the AOA vanes are static with no air passing over them, it is normal to observe the values fluctuate from wind, people movement on the airplane, and vibration from engine runs. NOTE: When the angle of attack probe test fixture, SPL-1917 is not available, follow the alternate procedures to test the AOA sensor. (2) When testing the AOA sensor output signals to the ADIRU and SMYD, complete the test on the same AOA sensor before testing the other sensor.

IF THE HEATER CIRCUIT BREAKERS ARE CLOSED, INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (9) Make sure that the AOA vane moves smooth from stop to stop and there is no visible damage. (a) Move the AOA vane from stop to stop. 1) Put the vane in position against one stop, then lightly tap the vane to cause movement to the other stop. a) Make sure that the vane moves smoothly through a range of approximately 200 degrees with just a light resistance caused by the viscous damper. NOTE: The vane movement gives the condition of the unit. For a satisfactory unit, the vane moves smoothly and the viscous damper will not let the vane touch the opposite stop. In a damaged unit, the vane moves easily with no resistance and hits the opposite stop, or a mechanical failure locks the mechanism. b) If the vane does not move smoothly from stop to stop, do one of the following steps: <1> Do the remaining steps in this task: Angle of Attack Sensor - Inspection, TASK 34-21-05-200-801. <2> Replace the AOA sensor, do these tasks: ANGLE OF ATTACK SENSOR - REMOVAL/INSTALLATION, PAGEBLOCK 34-21-05/401. (b) Visually examine AOA sensor for signs of any physical damage. 1) If physical damage is found, do this task: Angle of Attack Sensor - Inspection, TASK 34-21-05-200-801.

(c) Move and hold the applicable AOA sensor vane, trailing edge down, to align with the center of the second screw down from the AOA sensor alignment pin hole. (Figure 501) 1) Make sure that the value displayed on the applicable SMYD is between the limits. a) Limits: -66.5° to -68.5°. SUBTASK 34-21-05-740-021 (7) If the AOA sensor does not meet the limits, do the AOA sensor test (SMYD) preferred method using angle of attack probe test fixture, SPL-1917. SUBTASK 34-21-05-860-040 (8) Push the ON/OFF switch on the SMYD.

K. AOA Sensor (Alpha Vane) Heater Test

SUBTASK 34-21-05-710-001 (1) Do these steps to test the left alpha vane: 34-21-05 (a) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name C 3 C01072 HEATERS ALPHA VANE LEFT (b) Set the PROBE HEAT A switch to the ON position. 1) Make sure that the L ALPHA VANE light goes off and the R ALPHA VANE light stays on. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH AIR DATA SENSORS WHEN HOT . A HOT AIR DATA SENSOR CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (c) Make sure that only the left alpha vane is heating by using one of these methods: 1) Measure the temperature of the sensor with an infrared or contact thermometer. 2) Look at the sensor with an infrared or thermal imager. (d) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name C 3 C01072 HEATERS ALPHA VANE LEFT (e) Make sure that the L ALPHA VANE, R ALPHA VANE, ANTI-ICE, and Master Caution lights are on. (f) Make sure that the left alpha vane is no longer heating. (g) Push to reset either Master Caution light. 1) Make sure that the Master Caution and ANTI-ICE annunciator lights go off. (h) Set the PROBE HEAT A switch to the AUTO position. SUBTASK 34-21-05-710-002 (2) Do these steps to test the right alpha vane: (a) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name D 3 C01071 HEATERS ALPHA VANE RIGHT (b) Set the PROBE HEAT B switch to the ON position. 1) Make sure that the R ALPHA VANE light goes off and the L ALPHA VANE light stays on. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH AIR DATA SENSORS WHEN HOT . A HOT AIR DATA SENSOR CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (c) Make sure that only the right alpha vane is heating by using one of these methods: 1) Measure the temperature of the sensor with an infrared or contact thermometer. 2) Look at the sensor with an infrared or thermal imager. 34-21-05 (d) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name D 3 C01071 HEATERS ALPHA VANE RIGHT (e) Make sure that the L ALPHA VANE, R ALPHA VANE, ANTI-ICE, and Master Caution lights are on. (f) Make sure that the right alpha vane is no longer heating. (g) Push to reset either Master Caution light. 1) Make sure the Master Caution and ANTI-ICE annunciator lights go off. (h) Set the PROBE HEAT B switch to the AUTO position.

E. Angle of Attack Sensor Inspection

SUBTASK 34-21-05-280-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE AOA HEAT IS NOT ON. IF YOU DO NOT , INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (1) Make sure that Angle of Attack (AOA) probe heat is off. SUBTASK 34-21-05-280-002 (2) Move the AOA vane from stop to stop. (a) Put the vane in position against one stop, then lightly tap the vane to cause movement to the other stop. 1) Make sure that the vane moves smoothly through a range of approximately 200 degrees with just a light resistance caused by the viscous damper. NOTE: The vane movement gives the condition of the unit. For a satisfactory unit, the vane moves smoothly and the viscous damper will not let the vane touch the opposite stop. In a damaged unit, the vane moves easily with no resistance and hits the opposite stop, or a mechanical failure locks the mechanism. SUBTASK 34-21-05-280-003 (3) Make sure that the vane counterweight of the AOA sensor does not stick against the upper vane end stop. (a) Turn the vane in an upward direction and put it against the vane end stop. (b) Hold the vane firmly against the vane end stop by hand for 3 seconds, then release. (c) Put the measurement arm of the force gauge, STD-19829, against the AOA vane at the base of the upper trailing edge. (d) As slowly as possible, move the vane away from the vane upper end stop position with the force gauge, STD-19829. 1) Make sure that you move the vane about 30 to 50 degrees at a time. 2) Make sure that the force gauge, STD-19829, is aligned with the vane. 3) Make sure that only the force gauge, STD-19829, moves the vane. (e) Record the results. 1) Make sure that the force gauge, STD-19829, reading is less than 0.026 lb (12 g). a) If the force gauge, STD-19829, reading is more than 0.026 lb (12 g), replace the AOA sensor, do these tasks: • Angle of Attack Sensor Removal, TASK 34-21-05-000-801 • Angle of Attack Sensor Installation, TASK 34-21-05-400-801. SUBTASK 34-21-05-280-010 (4) Make sure that the vane counterweight of the AOA sensor does not stick against the lower vane end stop. (a) Turn the vane downward and put it against the vane end stop. (b) Hold the vane firmly against the vane end stop by hand for 3 seconds, then release. (c) Put the measurement arm of the force gauge, STD-19829, against the AOA vane at the base of the lower trailing edge. 34-21-05 (d) As slowly as possible, move the vane away from the vane lower end stop position with the force gauge, STD-19829. 1) Make sure that you move the vane about 30 to 50 degrees at a time. 2) Make sure that the force gauge, STD-19829, is aligned with the vane. 3) Make sure that only the force gauge, STD-19829, moves the vane. (e) Record the results. 1) Make sure that the force gauge, STD-19829, reading is less than 0.026 lb (12 g). a) If the force gauge, STD-19829, reading is more than 0.026 lb (12 g), replace the AOA sensor, do these tasks: • Angle of Attack Sensor Removal, TASK 34-21-05-000-801 • Angle of Attack Sensor Installation, TASK 34-21-05-400-801. SUBTASK 34-21-05-280-017 (5) Examine the vane upper, lower, and outward facing surfaces for theses conditions: (a) Looks for nicks, abrasions, and scratches. NOTE: Discoloration and/or cosmetic marks on the vane coating are permitted. (b) If the damage goes through the surface, replace the AOA sensor, do these tasks: • Angle of Attack Sensor Removal, TASK 34-21-05-000-801 • Angle of Attack Sensor Installation, TASK 34-21-05-400-801. SUBTASK 34-21-05-280-018 (6) Examine the trailing edge for these conditions: (a) Look for nicks or wear that cause the edge to be rounded or chamfered. NOTE: The edge must remain sharp and no deformation or removal of material is permitted. NOTE: Discoloration or cosmetic marks on the surface are permitted. (b) If damage is found, replace the AOA sensor, do these tasks: • Angle of Attack Sensor Removal, TASK 34-21-05-000-801 • Angle of Attack Sensor Installation, TASK 34-21-05-400-801. SUBTASK 34-21-05-280-019 (7) Examine the leading edge for these conditions: (a) Erosion or nicks with a depth of more than 0.1 in. (2.5 mm). (b) If damage is found, replace the AOA sensor, do these tasks: • Angle of Attack Sensor Removal, TASK 34-21-05-000-801 • Angle of Attack Sensor Installation, TASK 34-21-05-400-801. SUBTASK 34-21-05-210-002 (8) Examine the faceplate/slinger for these conditions: (a) Scratches or nicks on the faceplate/slinger are permitted. NOTE: Surface marks/scratches do not change the vane aerodynamic performance or the structural integrity of the faceplate. SUBTASK 34-21-05-000-001 (9) If the vane was known to be hit and has no visual external damage, do these steps: (a) Do this task: Angle of Attack Sensor Removal, TASK 34-21-05-000-801. 34-21-05 (b) Send it to a repair facility for tests and analysis to make sure that there is no internal damage. (c) Install a new AOA sensor, do this task: Angle of Attack Sensor Installation, TASK 34-21-05-400-801. SUBTASK 34-21-05-280-016 (10) Return the vane to a horizontal position. F . Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition SUBTASK 34-21-05-860-004 (1) For the left AOA, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name E 8 C00425 ADIRU LEFT EXC CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name C 3 C01072 HEATERS ALPHA VANE LEFT SUBTASK 34-21-05-860-026 (2) For the right AOA, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name D 3 C01071 HEATERS ALPHA VANE RIGHT F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name C 15 C00426 ADIRU RIGHT EXC

H. TAT Probe Installation

NOTE: The following procedure is for installing an aspirated TAT probe in airplanes configured for an aspirated TAT probe, and for installing non-aspirated TAT probe in airplanes configured for non-aspirated TAT probe. SUBTASK 34-21-06-860-002 (1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open and has safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name C 2 C00238 HEATERS TEMP PROBE SUBTASK 34-21-06-110-001 (2) Clean and prepare the surface and sides of the installation hole, do this task: Clean Bare, Clad, or Plated Metal with Solvent, TASK 20-10-34-110-802. SUBTASK 34-21-06-420-001 (3) Do these steps to install the TAT probe [4]: 34-21-06 (a) Put the new gasket [2] into its position on the TAT probe [4]. NOTE: It is not necessary to fit a new gasket if acquiring one will cause a flight delay. The old gasket, if in good condition, can be reused and replaced with a new gasket in one week or less. (b) Remove the protective cap from the electrical connector [1]. (c) Examine the electrical connector [1] for loose, bent, or broken pins. (d) Connect the electrical connector [1] to the TAT probe [4]. (e) Carefully put the TAT probe [4] into its position. NOTE: The large intake must point forward. 1) Make sure that remove caps and examine pins before installation. (f) Install the screws [3] that hold the TAT probe [4] to the airplane. (g) Tighten the screws [3] to 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m) - 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m). SUBTASK 34-21-06-760-001 (4) Do these steps to complete the bonding measurement check: (a) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the body of the TAT probe [4] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. 2) Make sure that the resistance is 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm) or less. (b) If the resistance is more than 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm), do these steps: 1) Remove the TAT probe [4]. 2) Clean the bonding surfaces, including the countersunk holes in the TAT probe [4] (SWPM 20-20-00). 3) Replace the screws [3] with new screws [3]. 4) Install the TAT probe [4]. 5) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the body of the TAT probe [4] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). a) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. b) Make sure that the resistance is 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm) or less. 6) If the resistance is more than 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm), do these steps: a) Remove the TAT probe [4]. b) Replace the nutplates and rivets that attach the TAT probe [4] (SRM 51-40-02). c) Install the TAT probe [4]. d) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the body of the TAT probe [4] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). <1> Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. <2> Make sure that the resistance is 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm) or less. 34-21-06 SUBTASK 34-21-06-390-001 (5) Apply sealant, A00247, around the TAT probe [4]. NOTE: It is not necessary to apply the sealant immediately, if the cure time will cause a flight delay. But, you must apply the sealant as soon as possible to keep moisture out of the area between the probe and airplane skin. The sealant must not wait more than a maximum of eight weeks to apply. SUBTASK 34-21-06-860-003 (6) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name C 2 C00238 HEATERS TEMP PROBE

I. Aspirated TAT Probe in Airplanes Configured with a Non-Aspirated TAT Probe Installation

NOTE: The following procedure is for installing an aspirated TAT probe in place of a non-aspirated TAT probe, and addresses capping the non-used probe bleed line, as well as gaining access to the back of the probe installation to permit access for connecting the electrical connector after positioning the probe onto the side of the fuselage. SUBTASK 34-21-06-860-008 (1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open and has safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name C 2 C00238 HEATERS TEMP PROBE SUBTASK 34-21-06-010-001 (2) If necessary, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 113BW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel (a) Do this task: Nose Wheel Well Access Panels - Removal, TASK 53-14-01-020-801. SUBTASK 34-21-06-110-002 (3) To clean and prepare the surface and sides of the installation hole, do this task: Clean Bare, Clad, or Plated Metal with Solvent, TASK 20-10-34-110-802. SUBTASK 34-21-06-420-002 (4) Do these steps to install an aspirated TAT probe [4] into an airplane configured for a non-aspirated TAT probe: (a) Put a cap assembly [6] on the ejector fitting [5]. 1) Tighten the cap assembly [6] to 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m) - 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m). (b) Put the new gasket [2] into its position on the TAT probe [4]. NOTE: It is not necessary to fit a new gasket if acquiring one will cause a flight delay. The old gasket, if in good condition, can be reused and replaced with a new gasket in one week or less. (c) Gain access to the back of the TAT probe [4], do this step: 1) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 113BW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel (d) Remove the protective cap from the electrical connector [1]. 34-21-06 (e) Examine the electrical connector [1] for loose, bent, or broken pins. (f) Carefully put the TAT probe [4] into its position. NOTE: The large intake should point forward. (g) Install the screws [3] that hold the TAT probe [4] to the airplane. (h) Tighten the screws [3] to 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m) - 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m). (i) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the body of the TAT probe [4] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. 2) Make sure that the resistance is less than 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm). (j) If the resistance is more than 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm), do these steps: 1) Remove the TAT probe [4]. 2) Clean the bonding surfaces, including the countersunk holes in the TAT probe [4] (SWPM 20-20-00). 3) Replace the screws [3] with new screws [3]. 4) Install the TAT probe [4]. 5) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the body of the TAT probe [4] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). a) Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. b) Make sure that the resistance is less than 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm). 6) If the resistance is more than 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm), do these steps: a) Remove the TAT probe [4]. b) Replace the nutplates and rivets that attach the TAT probe [4] (SRM 51-40-02). c) Install the TAT probe [4]. d) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the body of the TAT probe [4] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). <1> Use a non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614. <2> Make sure that the resistance is 0.010 ohms (10 milliohm) or less. (k) Connect the electrical connector [1] to the TAT probe [4] receptacle as follows: 1) Gain access to the back of the TAT probe [4] from access panel in the nose wheel well. (l) Apply sealant, A00247, around the TAT probe [4]. NOTE: It is not necessary to apply the sealant, A00247, immediately, if the cure time will cause a flight delay. But, you must apply the sealant as soon as possible to keep moisture out of the area between the probe and airplane skin. The sealant application must not wait more than a maximum of eight weeks. SUBTASK 34-21-06-410-002 (5) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 113BW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel (a) Do this task: Nose Wheel Well Access Panels - Installation, TASK 53-14-01-420-801. 34-21-06 SUBTASK 34-21-06-860-009 (6) Close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name C 2 C00238 HEATERS TEMP PROBE

J. TAT System Test

SUBTASK 34-21-06-730-001 (1) Do this task: Pitot Probe, AOA Sensor, and TAT Probe Heater - System Test, TASK 30-31-00-730-801. SUBTASK 34-21-06-860-005 (2) Do these steps to get access the Air Data Inertial Reference System (ADIRS) maintenance index on the Control Display Unit (CDU): NOTE: CDU data lines that permit a selection are identified with a caret (< or >). The CDU has 12 line-select-keys. Six keys are on each side of the display. 1L thru 6L are on the left side, and 1R thru 6R are on the right side. (a) Push the INIT REF key. 1) Make sure that the CDU shows the INIT REF INDEX 1/1 page. (b) Push the LSK 6R adjacent to the MAINT> prompt on the CDU. 1) Make sure that the CDU shows the MAINT BITE INDEX 1/1 page. SUBTASK 34-21-06-710-002 (3) Do these steps to get access the left ADIRS current faults: (a) Set the IRS MSU left mode select switch to NAV position. (b) Push the LSK 1L adjacent to the <ADIRS L prompt on the CDU. 1) Make sure that the CDU shows the ADIRS L BITE MAIN MENU page. (c) Push the LSK 1L adjacent to the <CURRENT STATUS prompt on the CDU. 1) Make sure that the CDU shows the ADIRS L BITE CURRENT FAULTS page. 2) Make sure that the CDU does not show the TAT PROBE SIGNAL FAIL message. NOTE: If there is a maintenance message that shows on the CDU, you can go to the ADIRS fault isolation procedures to repair the fault FIM 34-21 TASK 813. SUBTASK 34-21-06-710-003 (4) Do these steps to access the right ADIRS current faults. (a) Set the IRS MSU right mode select switch to NAV position. (c) Push the LSK 1L adjacent to the <CURRENT STATUS prompt on the CDU. 1) Make sure that the CDU shows the ADIRS R BITE CURRENT FAULTS page. 34-21-06 2) Make sure that the CDU does not show the TAT PROBE SIGNAL FAIL message. NOTE: If there is a maintenance message that shows on the CDU, you can go to the ADIRS fault isolation procedure to fix the fault FIM 34-21 TASK 813.

SUBTASK 34-21-06-860-006 (1) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name C 2 C00238 HEATERS TEMP PROBE

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-21-06-200-001 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE TAT PROBE HEAT IS OFF . THE PROBE BECOMES HOT IF IT IS ON. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (1) Visually examine the Total Air T emperature (TAT) probe of the air inlet scoop and air exit ports for blockages caused by unwanted material. (a) Make sure that air passes freely through the tube. 1) If there is unwanted material, contamination, or Foreign Object Debris (FOD), then replace the TAT probe. These are the tasks: Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801 Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801 (2) Visually examine the sensor for physical damage such as cracking or separation of parts on the air scoop and strut. (a) If there is any cracking or separation visible, then replace the TAT probe. These are the tasks: Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801 Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801 34-21-06 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH ASPIRATED TAT PROBES (3) Check for wear and indentations greater than 0.17 in. (4.32 mm) deep, measured from the leading edge of the strut. When measuring from the trailing edge of the strut, any measurement less than 1.83 in. (46.48 mm) is unacceptable. (a) If there is any cracking or separation visible, then replace the TAT probe. These are the tasks: Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801 Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH NON-ASPIRATED TAT PROBES (4) Check for wear and indentations greater than 0.08 in. (2.03 mm) deep, measured from the leading edge of the strut. When measuring from the trailing edge of the strut, any measurement less than 1.57 in. (39.88 mm) is unacceptable. (a) If there is any cracking or separation visible, then replace the TAT probe. These are the tasks: Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801 Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH ASPIRATED TAT PROBES (5) Check for wear and indentations greater than 0.04 in. (1.02 mm) deep, measured from the front of scoop. When measuring from back of scoop, any measurement less than 2.11 in. (53.59 mm) is unacceptable. (a) If there is any cracking or separation visible, then replace the TAT probe. These are the tasks: Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801 Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH NON-ASPIRATED TAT PROBES (6) Check for wear and indentations greater than 0.04 in. (1.02 mm) deep, measured from the front of scoop. When measuring from back of scoop, any measurement less than 3.46 in. (87.88 mm) is unacceptable. (a) If there is any cracking or separation visible, then replace the TAT probe. These are the tasks: Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801 Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801 (7) Visually check the interior of the air scoop to see if the airbump has worn away. The sensor is serviceable regardless of condition of airbump as long as it is present. (a) If the airbump has worn away, then replace the TAT probe. These are the tasks: Total Air T emperature Probe - Removal, TASK 34-21-06-000-801 Total Air T emperature Probe - Installation, TASK 34-21-06-400-801 ALL 34-21-06

E. Standby Compass Calibrator (SCC) Adjustment

SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-001 (1) Calibrate the Standby Compass Calibrator (SCC) (standby compass calibration kit, COM-1925) to the magnetic field at the location of the compass swing area, do these steps: (a) Put a tripod, STD-1167, at the center of the compass swing area. (b) Remove the magnet assembly from the SCC. (c) Remove the knob assembly from the SCC. (d) Attach a master magnetic compass to the SCC with two mounting screws. NOTE: It is possible to use an accurate standby magnetic compass for a master magnetic compass. 1) Make sure that the N-S and E-W adjustment screws are at neutral. (e) Put the SCC/master compass assembly on the tripod, STD-1167. 1) Make sure that the assembly is level. (f) Turn the assembly until the master magnetic compass shows an indication of magnetic north (N). (g) Re-install the magnet assembly to the SCC. (h) Re-install the knob assembly to the SCC. (i) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of E at the index line. (j) Make a record of the heading shown on the master magnetic compass. (k) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of W at the index line. (l) Make a record of the heading shown on the master magnetic compass. (m) Turn the magnetic field cancellation adjustment screw on the SCC to decrease the heading errors in each direction (E and W) to a minimum. (n) Continue to adjust the SCC dials for each direction (E and W). 1) Use the Magnetic Field Cancellation Adjustment (MFCA) screw until the errors are at a minimum. NOTE: Continue to do this procedure until the error in each direction is at a minimum. When the errors are at a minimum, do not move the MFCA screw until the compass swing is completed. (o) Remove the master magnetic compass from the SCC. 34-23-00 F . Four Point Calibration Swing SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-101 (1) Position the airplane in the compass swing area: (a) To taxi the airplane, do this task: T axi the Airplane, TASK 09-20-00-580-801. (b) To tow the airplane, do this task: Maintenance Towing, TASK 09-11-00-580-801. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-102 (2) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name C 1 C00523 HEATERS CAPT PITOT C 2 C00238 HEATERS TEMP PROBE C 3 C01072 HEATERS ALPHA VANE LEFT C 4 C00236 HEATERS ELEV PITOT LEFT D 3 C01071 HEATERS ALPHA VANE RIGHT D 4 C00237 HEATERS ELEV PITOT RIGHT D 5 C00525 HEATERS F/O PITOT D 6 C00524 HEATERS AUX PITOT 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-168, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 169 POST SB 737-30A1063 D 8 C01946 PROBE AUTO HEAT CAPT D 9 C01947 PROBE AUTO HEAT F/O ALL E 3 C00234 HEATERS DRAIN MAST GND E 4 C00700 HEATERS DRAIN MAST AIR E 5 C00233 HEATERS DRAIN SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-002 (3) Energize all of the electronic equipment, radios, and flight compartment lights for the usual conditions that occur in flight. (a) The Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) and Weather Radar must be disengaged or off. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-103 WARNING PREPARE THE SAFETY-SENSITIVE SYSTEMS FOR THE AIR MODE BEFORE YOU INSTALL THE DEACTUATORS. IN THE AIR MODE, MANY OF THE AIRPLANE SYSTEMS CAN OPERATE. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (4) Do this task: Prepare to Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-840-801. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-104 (5) Attach an actuator on the Ground Spoiler Interlock Valve Proximity Sensor (S1050). NOTE: The actuator is a part of the proximity sensor test set, SPL-1690. For information on the Ground Spoiler Interlock Valve Proximity Sensor, refer to this task: Ground Spoiler Interlock Valve Proximity Sensor Functional Test, TASK 27-62-61-400-806. 34-23-00 SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-105 (6) Attach the deactuators to the face of the air/ground sensors for the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. NOTE: The installation of the deactuators will energize the landing gear latch solenoid. Because the landing gear latch solenoid is close to the standby magnetic compass, the solenoid must be energized to create a normal level of magnetic and electrical interference during calibration of the compass. (a) Let the landing gear latch solenoid stay energized for 20 minutes before you continue. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-003 (7) Set the ND mode selector, on the left Electronic Flight Instrument System (EFIS) control panel, on the glareshield, to the VOR position or to the ILS position. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-017 (8) Lower the mounting bracket for the standby magnetic compass to give sufficient space for the SCC: (a) Loosen the screws on the mounting bracket to let it tilt down. (b) Move the mounting bracket to you and approximately 15 degrees down. (c) Tighten the screws on the mounting bracket. SUBTASK 34-23-00-020-001 (9) Remove the lower left and upper right mounting screws on the standby magnetic compass. SUBTASK 34-23-00-480-001 (10) Use the two mounting screws to install the SCC on the face of the standby magnetic compass. SUBTASK 34-23-00-020-002 (11) Disconnect the electrical connectors from the standby magnetic compass. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-003 (12) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of E at the index line. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-001 (13) Make a record of the heading shown on the standby magnetic compass. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-004 (14) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of W at the index line. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-002 (15) Make a record of the heading shown on the standby magnetic compass. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-005 (16) Turn the E-W adjustment screw on the standby magnetic compass until the error in the last two recorded values is at a minimum. NOTE: Divide the error in each of the two directions as equally as possible. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-006 (17) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of N at the index line. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-003 (18) Make a record of the heading shown on the standby magnetic compass. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-007 (19) Turn the top and bottom SCC dials to show an indication of S at the index line. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-004 (20) Make a record of the heading shown on the standby magnetic compass. 34-23-00 SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-008 (21) Turn the N-S adjustment screw on the standby magnetic compass until the error in the last two recorded values is at a minimum. NOTE: Divide the error in each of the two directions as equally as possible. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-009 (22) Continue to adjust the SCC dials for each pair of directions (E-W, N-S). (a) Turn the E-W and N-S adjustment screws until the errors are at a minimum. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-019 (23) Continue to do this procedure until the error in each pair of directions is at a minimum. (a) Start with E-W and turn the E-W adjustment screw. (b) Do N-S and turn the N-S adjustment screw. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-010 (24) When the errors are at a minimum, do the steps that follow for the twelve point accuracy swing.

G. Twelve Point Accuracy Swing and Compass Correction Card

SUBTASK 34-23-00-580-003 (1) Move the airplane to a location near the center of the compass swing area. NOTE: For each of the magnetic headings that follow, the remaining deviation for the standby magnetic compass must not be more than ±5 degrees. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-011 (2) Adjust the SCC dials to indicate these magnetic headings: 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 210, 240, 270, 300, and 330 degrees. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-005 (3) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, MH, and the standby compass heading, CH, for each 30 degree increment. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-111 (4) Put the compass correction card, STD-7061, next to the compass. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-006 (5) Make a record of the standby compass heading, CH, in the steer column of the compass correction card, STD-7061, for each 30 degree heading increment. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-020 (6) If the remaining deviation measurement is greater than 5 degrees, do one or more of these steps: (a) Do this task: Standby Magnetic Compass - Degaussing, TASK 34-23-00-820-803. (b) Confirm there are no magnetic influences near the compass that could be impacting the measurements such as non-essential ground equipment, non-ferrous material, cell phone or laptop near the compass. NOTE: A cell phone can affect compass readings. Cell phones emit electromagnetic fields, which can interfere with the magnetic field sensed by a compass and cause it to give incorrect readings. 34-23-00 SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-032 (7) If a remaining deviation measurement is greater than the local regulatory accuracy requirement, replace the Standby Magnetic Compass (TASK 34-23-00-000-801 and TASK 34-23-00-400-801). NOTE: Most regulations state the compensated installation may not have a deviation, in level flight, greater than 10 degrees on any heading.

(b) Remove the SCC. (c) Install and tighten the mounting screws on the standby magnetic compass. NOTE: The installation of the deactuators will energize the landing gear latch solenoid. Because the landing gear latch solenoid is close to the standby magnetic compass, the solenoid must be energized to create a normal level of magnetic and electrical interference during calibration of the compass. (a) Let the landing gear latch solenoid stay energized for 20 minutes before you continue. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-010 (10) Set the ND mode selector, on the left Electronic Flight Instrument System (EFIS) control panel, on the glareshield, to the VOR position or to the ILS position. (11) Make sure that the N-S and E-W adjustment screws on the standby compass are at neutral. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-117 (12) Turn the airplane to Magnetic North 000 deg using (a) or (b) for target magnetic heading. (a) The ISDU true heading plus (+E) or minus (-W) the site magnetic declination angle. (b) The compass rose heading mark. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-007 (13) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, (MH)n, and the standby compass heading, (CH)n. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-008 (14) Calculate and make a record of the north heading deviation, Dn, as follows: Dn = (MH)n - (CH)n. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-118 (15) Turn the airplane to Magnetic East 090 deg using (a) or (b) for target magnetic heading. (a) The ISDU true heading plus (+E) or minus (-W) the site magnetic declination angle. (b) The compass rose heading mark. 34-23-00 SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-009 (16) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, (MH)e, and the standby compass heading, (CH)e. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-010 (17) Calculate and make a record of the east heading deviation, De, as follows: De = (MH)e - (CH)e. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-119 (18) Turn the airplane to Magnetic South 180 deg using (a) or (b) for target magnetic heading. (a) The ISDU true heading plus (+E) or minus (-W) the site magnetic declination angle. (b) The compass rose heading mark. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-011 (19) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, (MH)s, and the standby compass heading, (CH)s. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-012 (20) Calculate and make a record of the south heading deviation, Ds, as follows: Ds = (MH)s - (CH)s. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-013 (21) Calculate and make a record of the north-south single-cycle error coefficient, C, and its sign as follows: C = 0.5(Dn - Ds). SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-013 (22) Turn the N-S adjustment screw on the standby compass (while at the south magnetic heading) to give a compass heading indication of (CH)s - C. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-120 (23) Turn the airplane to Magnetic West 270 deg using (a) or (b) for target magnetic heading. (a) The ISDU true heading plus (+E) or minus (-W) the site magnetic declination angle. (b) The compass rose heading mark. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-014 (24) Make a record of the target magnetic heading, (MH)w, and the standby compass heading, (CH)w. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-015 (25) Calculate and make a record of the west heading deviation, Dw, as follows: Dw = (MH)w - (CH)w. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-016 (26) Calculate and make a record of the east-west single-cycle error coefficient, B, and its sign as follows: B = 0.5(De - Dw). SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-014 (27) Turn the E-W adjustment screw on the standby compass (while at the west magnetic heading) to give a compass heading indication of (CH)w - B. F . Twelve Point Correction Swing Procedure SUBTASK 34-23-00-580-009 (1) Move the airplane to a location near the center of the compass swing area. SUBTASK 34-23-00-970-018 (4) Calculate the deviation, D, for each 30 degree heading as follows: D = MH - CH. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-121 (6) Put the compass correction card, STD-7061, next to the compass. (b) Confirm there are no magnetic influences near the compass that could be impacting the measurements such as non-essential ground equipment, non-ferrous material, cell phone or laptop near the compass. NOTE: A cell phone can affect compass readings. Cell phones emit electromagnetic fields, which can interfere with the magnetic field sensed by a compass and cause it to give incorrect readings. SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-031 (8) If a remaining deviation measurement is greater than the local regulatory accuracy requirement, replace the Standby Magnetic Compass (TASK 34-23-00-000-801 and TASK 34-23-00-400-801). NOTE: Most regulations state the compensated installation may not have a deviation, in level flight, greater than 10 degrees on any heading.

34-23-00-820-803Standby Magnetic Compass - DegaussingPDF p. 440

7. Standby Magnetic Compass - Degaussing (Figure 203)

A. General

(1) Use tools that are not magnetic to adjust the standby magnetic compass.

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-4745 Compass - Handheld STD-6158 Coil - Demagnetizing, AC

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Prepare for Standby Magnetic Compass Degaussing

SUBTASK 34-23-00-840-003 (1) Precautions necessary to demagnetize the standby compass are as follows: (a) Do not permit the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 to remain within 10 ft (3.05 m) of any part of aircraft unless it is energized. (b) Do not operate the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 in vicinity of magnetic compass. (c) Care should be taken to ensure that the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 is not actually in contact with surface when used. (To be effective, it should be used as close to surface as possible.)

E. Standby Magnetic Compass Degaussing Procedure.

SUBTASK 34-23-00-820-017 (1) Find and identify the area to be demagnetized as follows: (a) Move a Handheld Compass, STD-4745, into the area adjacent to the standby compass. 1) Make sure that the needle of the Handheld Compass, STD-4745, points to magnetic north before using it. (b) If the Handheld Compass, STD-4745, needle moves away from magnetic north, identify the area for demagnetization. (2) Demagnetize the standby compass area to restore to normal configuration (area about windshields and flight compartment) as follows: (Figure 203) (a) Deactivate the standby magnetic compass. Do this task: Standby Magnetic Compass - Deactivation, TASK 34-23-00-040-801. (b) Remove the standby compass and store it in an area away from the aircraft. (c) Energize the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 at a distance of at least 10 ft (3.05 m) from the aircraft. 34-23-00 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU OBEY THE PROCEDURES TO REMOVE THE MAGNETIC PARTICLES FROM THE WINDSHIELD AND THE FLIGHT COMPARTMENT AREAS. KEEP THE TOOL ABOVE THE LOWER PART OF THE WINDSHIELD SILLS. THIS WILL PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE INSTRUMENTS. (d) Move the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 slowly towards windshield areas, bring the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 as close as possible to the structure without touching the structure. Move it in series of parallel strokes over the entire windshield area. NOTE: The windshield area is defined as the area from top of windshield aft for a distance of 36 in. (914.4 mm), bounded on each side by the left and right sliding windshields. (e) Demagnetize the windshield screws by moving the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 in line with the screws. (f) Slowly withdraw the AC demagnetizing coil, STD-6158 at least 10 ft (3.05 m) from the aircraft before deenergizing. (g) Check the areas that are degaussed with a Handheld Compass, STD-4745 for signs of any remaining magnetization. If magnetization still exists, repeat process of degaussing until evidence of magnetization disappears. (h) When the area is satisfactorily demagnetized, install the standby compass. (i) Activate the standby magnetic compass. Do this task: Standby Magnetic Compass - Activation, TASK 34-23-00-440-801. SUBTASK 34-23-00-700-002 (3) Do a check of the standby magnetic compass system. Do this task: Standby Magnetic Compass - Compass Rose or Inertial Reference System (IRS) Method, TASK 34-23-00-820-802 or Standby Magnetic Compass Swing - Standby Compass Calibrator (SCC) Method, TASK 34-23-00-820-801. F . Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition SUBTASK 34-23-00-940-001 (1) Remove all the tools and equipment from the work area. Make sure the area is clean.

SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-027 (1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open and has safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name A 14 C00161 CONTROL CABIN LIGHTING STBY COMPASS SUBTASK 34-23-00-420-002 CAUTION USE ONLY TOOLS THAT ARE NOT MAGNETIC FOR THE REMOVAL AND THE INSTALLATION OF THE STANDBY MAGNETIC COMPASS. MAGNETIC TOOLS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE INSTRUMENT . (2) Install the standby magnetic compass [1]: (a) Remove the protective covers from the electrical connector [3] and the connector on the back of the standby magnetic compass [1]. (b) Examine the electrical connector [3] for bent or broken pins, dirt, and damage. (c) Install the standby magnetic compass [1] onto the mounting bracket. (d) Connect the electrical connector [3] to the standby magnetic compass [1]. 1) Push the electrical connector [3] until it locks into its position with a click. 34-23-00 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; AIRPLANES WITH AMETEK NON-MOD A COMPASS C-5L 2) Wind 1 inch wide Scotch No. 24 wire mesh tape around the junction of the electrical connector [3] and standby magnetic compass [1] a minimum of three times. NOTE: Securing the connector with tape only applies to AMETEK C-5L compass that has not been modified to MOD A. An “A” as a suffix to the serial number indicate a MOD A configuration. NOTE: The tape must touch against the rear of the standby magnetic compass case. Keep sufficient tension on the tape while you wind the junction to make it the shape of the connector. You can use thinner tape, if you wind the connector with a minimum overlap of 50 percent. Wind all parts of the connector within 1 inch of the compass with a minimum of three wrappings. T emporarily secure the end of the tape. 3) Wind the mesh tape a minimum of two times with 1 inch wide Scotch No. 70 or A-A-59163 Type I self-fusing silicone rubber tape. NOTE: Keep sufficient tension on the tape while you wind the junction to make it the shape of the connector You can use thinner tape, if you wind the connector with a minimum overlap of 50 percent. Wind all of the wire mesh tape with a minimum of two wrappings of the silicone rubber tape. 4) If the connector is removed for any reason, discard all tape and repeat step (d) above using new tape. ALL (e) Install the screws [2] at the corners of the standby magnetic compass [1]. SUBTASK 34-23-00-860-028 (3) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name A 14 C00161 CONTROL CABIN LIGHTING STBY COMPASS

2. Standby Attitude Reference System - System Test

A. References

Reference Title 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-197; AIRPLANES WITHOUT THE ALTERNATE NAVIGATION SYSTEM

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-001 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-003 (2) Set the mode selector switch on the standby attitude indicator to the OFF position. SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-004 (3) Let the gyro get to full speed. NOTE: The gyro will reach full speed approximately 3 minutes after you supply power. SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-006 (4) Pull and release the cage knob on the standby indicator. NOTE: Do not let the knob hit against the front of the indicator. SUBTASK 34-24-00-750-001 (5) After five minutes, make sure that the attitude data on the Standby Attitude Indicator is the same as the captain’s attitude display ± 2 degrees. SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-007 (6) Open this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name D 9 C01387 STBY ATT IND SUBTASK 34-24-00-750-002 (7) Make sure the GYRO flag comes into view in less than one second. 34-24-00 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-197; AIRPLANES WITHOUT THE ALTERNATE NAVIGATION SYSTEM (Continued) SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-008 (8) Close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name D 9 C01387 STBY ATT IND SUBTASK 34-24-00-750-004 (9) Make sure the GYRO flag goes out of view within 3 minutes. SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-009 (10) Tune the captain's VHF NAV receiver to the frequency of 108.35 MHz. NOTE: To set the frequency, turn the frequency selector until the selected frequency shows in the STANDBY display window. Then, push the TFR switch. The frequency will show in the ACTIVE display window. The frequency of 108.35 MHz is the test frequency for the ILS. SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-010 (11) Set the mode selector switch on the standby attitude indicator to the APP position. SUBTASK 34-24-00-740-001 (12) Push the TEST switch on the captain's VHF NAV control panel. (a) Make sure that the G/S and LOC flags come into view and then go out of view in less than five seconds. (b) Make sure the localizer deviation bar moves one mark left and the glide slope deviation bar moves one mark up. (c) Make sure the localizer deviation bar moves one mark right and the glide slope deviation bar moves one mark down. SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-011 (13) Set the mode selector switch on the standby attitude indicator to the B/CRS position. SUBTASK 34-24-00-740-003 (14) Push the TEST switch on the captain's VHF NAV control panel. (a) Make sure the LOC flag comes into view and then goes out of view in less than five seconds. (b) Make sure the glide slope deviation bar and the G/S flag are out of view. (c) Make sure the localizer deviation bar moves to the right side of the center and then to the left side of the center. SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-012 (15) Set the mode selector switch on the standby attitude indicator to the OFF position. SUBTASK 34-24-00-860-013 (16) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

C. Location Zones

D. Removal Procedure

SUBTASK 34-24-02-860-001 (1) Open this circuit breaker and attach a DO-NOT-CLOSE tag: (a) Front of the ISFD Dedicated Battery System, M2100, E4-1: 1) DBC Output breaker SUBTASK 34-24-02-860-020 (2) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name B 9 C00331 PANEL & INSTR 28V PRI CAPT & CTR D 8 C00701 EMER PANEL LTG SUBTASK 34-24-02-020-001 CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE CONNECTOR PINS OR OTHER CONDUCTORS ON THE INTEGRATED STANDBY FLIGHT DISPLAY . IF YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE INTEGRATED STANDBY FLIGHT DISPLAY . (3) Remove the integrated standby flight display [3]: (a) Loosen, but do not remove, the two adjustment screws [1] adjacent to the integrated standby flight display [3] until the integrated standby flight display [3] can be removed. 34-24-02 1) If necessary, push the two adjustment screws to release the ISFD from the mount clamp. CAUTION DO NOT USE THE BARO KNOB TO PULL THE DISPLAY [3] FROM THE INSTRUMENT PANEL. DAMAGE TO THE DISPLAY [3] CAN OCCUR IF THE BARO KNOB IS PULLED DURING REMOVAL. CAUTION CAREFULLY PULL THE DISPLAY [3] FROM THE INSTRUMENT PANEL. TOO MUCH FORCE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELECTRICAL CABLE AND THE HOSES ON THE REAR OF THE DISPLAY [3]. (b) Use the ISFD extracting tool, SPL-12596 to pull the integrated standby flight display [3] from the instrument panel until you can get access to the electrical connector [4], pitot hose [5] and static hose [6]. (c) If the integrated standby flight display [3] is not easy to remove, loosen the two mounting screws [2] to make the removal easier. (d) If necessary, remove the adjacent coverplate for more access to disconnect the electrical and pneumatic connectors. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE PITOT-STATIC SYSTEM IS AT AMBIENT PRESSURE BEFORE YOU DISCONNECT THE PITOT HOSE [5] AND THE STATIC HOSE [6]. IF THE PITOT-STATIC SYSTEM IS NOT AT AMBIENT PRESSURE, DAMAGE TO THE DISPLAY [3] CAN OCCUR. (e) Disconnect the pitot hose [5] and static hose [6] from the integrated standby flight display [3]. (f) Disconnect the electrical connector [4]. (g) Remove the integrated standby flight display [3]. (h) Do this task: Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover Installation, TASK 20-40-12-400-804.

IF YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ISFD DEDICATED BATTERY-CHARGER.
