(d) Connect the pitot hose [5] and static hose [6] to the integrated standby flight display [3]. 34-24-02 (e) Do a visual inspection to make sure the pitot-static system hose connections and quick-disconnect fittings are locked in the sealed position. 1) Make sure that the actuation ring of the quick-disconnect fitting is fully engaged on the lock pin and you see the colored lock ring indicator that shows a correct connection of the quick-disconnect fitting. (f) If you loosened the mounting screws, apply Loctite 222MS compound, A50212, or Loctite 222 compound, A00270, to the threads of the mounting screws [2]. (g) Install the integrated standby flight display [3] into the instrument panel. 1) Make sure that the ISFD is seated all the way into the panel opening. And pushed tight against the panel face with no gaps between the instrument bezel and the panel face. (h) Torque the two adjustment screws [1] adjacent to the integrated standby flight display [3] to 4 in-lb (5 kg-cm) - 9 in-lb (10 kg-cm). (i) If you loosened the mounting screws, torque the two mounting screws [2] to 4 in-lb (5 kg-cm) - 9 in-lb (10 kg-cm). (j) Do a visual inspection to make sure that the ISFD is properly fitted in its clamp and aligned with the cockpit panel. (k) Install the coverplate if previously removed. E. ISFD Installation Test

SUBTASK 34-24-02-860-004 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 34-24-02-860-019 (2) Do this task: Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the ISDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-802 or Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the FMC CDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-801 SUBTASK 34-24-02-700-007 CAUTION AIRPLANES WITH ISFD S231A120-1; DO NOT MOVE THE AIRPLANE WHILE THE ISFD SHOWS THE YELLOW "ATT" AND "INIT90S" MESSAGES. IF YOU MOVE THE AIRPLANE DURING THE ISFD SYSTEM POWER-UP AND INITIALIZATION ALIGNMENT , THE ISFD CAN SHOW INCORRECT ATTITUDE DATA WITH NO ATT FLAG OR MESSAGE. (3) Close this circuit breaker and remove the DO-NOT-CLOSE tag: (a) Front of the ISFD Dedicated Battery System, M2100, E4-1: 1) DBC Output Breaker 34-24-02 SUBTASK 34-24-02-700-001 (4) Make sure that the display shows the following flags in approximately 15 seconds after power up: (a) SPD flag (b) ATT flag (c) ALT flag (d) INIT 90S flag. SUBTASK 34-24-02-710-001 (5) Make sure that the following flags and indications show in approximately 15 to 90 seconds after power up: (a) ATT flag (b) INIT 90S flag (c) Airspeed indication with no SPD flag (d) Altitude indication with no ALT flag. SUBTASK 34-24-02-710-002 (6) Make sure that the following is displayed on the ISFD after approximately 90 seconds: (a) Attitude (normal) display with the following indications with no flags: 1) Fixed aircraft symbol 2) Roll scale 3) Roll index 4) Pitch scale. NOTE: To restart the initialization, push and release the ATT RST button on the face of the ISFD. SUBTASK 34-24-02-820-001 (7) Make sure that the attitude data on the ISFD is the same as the captain’s attitude display ± 1 degree. C. Prepare for the Operational Test

SUBTASK 34-24-02-860-017 (1) Supply power to the ISFD: (a) To use airplane power, do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. (b) To use battery power, set the battery switch S5 on the Electrical Meters, Battery, and Galley Power Module (p5-13) to “ON”.

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-24-02-700-009 (1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed: (a) Front of the ISFD Dedicated Battery System, M2100, E4-1: 1) DBC Output Breaker SUBTASK 34-24-02-710-006 (2) Do this task: Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the ISDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-802 or Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the FMC CDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-801. 34-24-02 SUBTASK 34-24-02-700-010 (3) Make sure that the display shows the following flags in approximately 15 seconds after power up: (a) SPD flag (b) ATT flag (c) ALT flag (d) INIT 90S flag. SUBTASK 34-24-02-710-004 (4) Make sure the following flags and indications show in approximately 15 to 90 seconds after power up: (a) ATT flag (b) INIT 90S flag (c) Airspeed indication with no SPD flag (d) Altitude indication with no ALT flag. SUBTASK 34-24-02-710-005 (5) Make sure the following is displayed on the ISFD after approximately 90 seconds: (a) Attitude (normal) display with the following indications with no flags: 1) Fixed aircraft symbol 2) Roll scale 3) Roll index 4) Pitch scale. NOTE: To restart the ATT , push and release the ATT RST button on the face of the ISFD.

E. Put the Airplane Back to its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 34-24-02-860-022 (1) Remove electrical power to the ISFD. (a) If applicable, do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812. (b) If applicable, set the battery switch S5 on the Electrical Meters, Battery, and Galley Power Module (p5-13) to “OFF”.

G. Installation of the Drain Coupling, 1QF2-3-64C (Recommended)

SUBTASK 34-24-02-480-001 WARNING WHEN THE STATIC PORTS ARE COVERED, MAKE SURE THAT CONDITION IS VISIBLE FROM THE GROUND. IN ADDITION, ATTACH A TAG TO THE LEFT CONTROL WHEEL IN THE FLIGHT DECK AS A REMINDER THAT THE STATIC PORTS ARE COVERED. FAILURE TO OBSERVE AND REMOVE COVERINGS OVER STATIC PORTS BEFORE FLIGHT MAY CAUSE LARGE ERRORS IN AIRSPEED-SENSING AND ALTITUDE-SENSING SIGNALS, WHICH MAY LEAD TO LOSS OF SAFE FLIGHT . CAUTION DO NOT PUSH THE TAPE INTO THE STATIC PORTS. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE STATIC SYSTEM IF YOU PUSH TAPE INTO THE STATIC PORT . (1) Seal the two alternate static ports with vinyl adhesive Scotch Brand No.471 tape, G02219 at these locations: (a) The ALTERNATE static port on the right side of the fuselage. (b) The ALTERNATE static port on the left side of the fuselage. SUBTASK 34-24-02-480-002 (2) Remove the cap from the No. 5 Alternate Static Drain, in the electronic equipment compartment, below the E-5 rack. Get access to the drain in the electronic equipment compartment through this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 34-24-02-400-001 (3) Install the coupling, COM-1927, on the No. 5 Alternate Static Drain. SUBTASK 34-24-02-400-002 (4) Connect the air data model test set, COM-1914 to the coupling, COM-1927.

SUBTASK 34-24-02-400-005 (2) Use the air data accessory kit, COM-25177, to connect the air data model test set, COM-1914, to the static test adapter, COM-1921. NOTE: The air data accessory kit, COM-25177, contains hoses to connect to the air data model test set, COM-1914, to the static test adapter, COM-1921. 34-24-02 SUBTASK 34-24-02-480-010 WARNING WHEN THE STATIC PORTS ARE COVERED, MAKE SURE THAT CONDITION IS VISIBLE FROM THE GROUND. SUBTASK 34-24-02-020-003 CAUTION THE CABIN ALTITUDE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE INDICATOR MUST BE DISCONNECTED FROM ITS STATIC PRESSURE SOURCE AND THE SOURCE CAPPED. (4) Disconnect the alternate static hose from the cabin altitude differential pressure Indicator located behind the P5 forward overhead panel.

SUBTASK 34-24-02-860-008 (1) Apply pressure to the alternate pitot and alternate static systems for each test point as shown in the table that follows (Table 501): (a) When you apply pressure to the static system, make sure that the rate is less than 5,000 feet for each minute. 34-24-02 (b) When you apply pressure to the pitot system, make sure that the rate is less than 300 knots for each minute. Hg) PITOT (mBar) ALTITUDE (feet) ALTITUDE (meters) AIRSPEED (knots) 1 29.921 1,013 30.311 1,026 0±30 0±9.14 90±3.5 2 24.896 843 27.996 948 5,000±50 1,524±15.24 250±3.5 3 16.886 572 17.703 599 15,000±110 4,572±33.52 130±3.5 4 11.104 376 17.013 576 25,000±160 7,620±48.76 340±8 5 7.041 238 10.963 371 35,000±210 10,668±64.00 279±6 6 5.286 179 7.95 269 41,000±235 12,496±71.62 233±6 SUBTASK 34-24-02-730-005 (2) At each test value, permit the pressure to become stable for one minute. (a) Do not hit or shake the display before you read the values. SUBTASK 34-24-02-780-001 (3) Make sure that the altitude and airspeed data on the ISFD is in tolerance for each test point in Table 501. SUBTASK 34-24-02-780-002 (4) Make sure that the attitude data on the ISFD is the same as the captain's attitude display ± 1 degree. SUBTASK 34-24-02-210-005 (5) Do a check to see if the ISFD dedicated battery System (E4-1) is operational: (a) Make sure that the red fault light on the front of the battery charger is not on. NOTE: The red fault light shows that the battery charger is not serviceable. The battery charger can be not serviceable because of battery temperature or because of a cell voltage problem. SUBTASK 34-24-02-860-009 (6) Put the system back to ambient pressure. (a) When you release the pressure from the static system, make sure that the rate is less than 5,000 feet for each minute. (b) When you release the pressure from the pitot system, make sure that the rate is less than 300 knots for each minute. IF THE PITOT-STATIC SYSTEM IS NOT AT AMBIENT PRESSURE, DAMAGE TO THE AIR DATA MODULES CAN OCCUR. (a) Disconnect the air data model test set, COM-1914 from the coupling, COM-1927. (b) Disconnect the coupling, COM-1927, from the No. 5 Alternate Static Drain. (c) Install the cap on the No. 5 Alternate Static Drain. 34-24-02 WARNING FAILURE TO REMOVE THE VINYL ADHESIVE TAPE FROM THE STATIC PORTS BEFORE FLIGHT CAN CAUSE LARGE ERRORS IN AIRSPEED- SENSING AND ALTITUDE-SENSING SIGNALS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN DANGEROUS FLIGHT . WARNING DO NOT FILL OR CHANGE THE HOLES IN THE PORT . MAKE SURE THAT YOU REMOVE ALL OF THE PIECES OF TAPE FROM THE STATIC PORTS. THE SURFACE OF THE PORT MUST BE SMOOTH AND CLEAN. IF IT IS NOT , THE SYSTEM WILL NOT OPERATE CORRECTLY AND IT CAN CAUSE INJURY . (d) Remove the Scotch Brand No.471 tape, G02219, from the alternate static ports at these locations: 1) The ALTERNATE static port on the right side of the fuselage. 2) The ALTERNATE static port on the left side of the fuselage. SUBTASK 34-24-02-480-008 (8) Removal of Static Port Adapter, static test adapter, COM-1921 CAUTION MAKE SURE THE PITOT-STATIC SYSTEM IS AT AMBIENT PRESSURE BEFORE YOU DISCONNECT THE TEST SET . IF THE PITOT-STATIC SYSTEM IS NOT AT AMBIENT PRESSURE, DAMAGE TO THE AIR DATA MODULES CAN OCCUR. (a) Disconnect the air data model test set, COM-1914 from the static test adapter, COM-1921. CAUTION REMOVE THE ADAPTER SLOWLY AND CAREFULLY . THE ADAPTER CAN CAUSE SCRATCHES ON THE STATIC PORT , WHICH CAN CAUSE FALSE ALTITUDE READINGS. (b) Remove the static test adapter, COM-1921, from the ALTERNATE static port on the left side of the fuselage. (c) Remove the Scotch Brand No.471 tape, G02219, from the ALTERNATE static port on the right side of the fuselage. SUBTASK 34-24-02-080-004 (9) Removal of the Pitot Probe Adapter CAUTION MAKE SURE THE PITOT-STATIC SYSTEM IS AT AMBIENT PRESSURE BEFORE YOU DISCONNECT THE TEST SET . IF THE PITOT-STATIC SYSTEM IS NOT AT AMBIENT PRESSURE, DAMAGE TO THE AIR DATA MODULES CAN OCCUR. (a) Disconnect the air data model test set, COM-1914 from the pitot test adapter, COM-1916. (b) Remove the pitot test adapter, COM-1916, from the pitot probe. SUBTASK 34-24-02-410-001 (10) Connect the alternate static hose to the cabin altitude differential pressure indicator located behind the P5 forward overhead panel. SUBTASK 34-24-02-210-007 (11) Do a visual inspection of the quick-disconnect fittings that you connected. 34-24-02 (a) Make sure that the actuation ring of the quick-disconnect fitting is fully engaged on the lock pins, and make sure that you see the colored lock ring indicator that shows a correct connection of the quick-disconnect fitting. SUBTASK 34-24-02-410-002 (12) Lift the P5 forward overhead panel to the closed position and turn the 1/4-turn fasteners.

4. ISFD Dedicated Battery System - Operational Test NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This task gives instruction to check if the battery charger and battery pack for the Integrated Standby Flight Display (ISFD) are operational.

B. References

Reference Title 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201)

Zone Area 117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left 118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right 121 Forward Cargo Compartment - Left 122 Forward Cargo Compartment - Right 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Prepare for the Operational Test

SUBTASK 34-24-02-860-014 (1) Make sure that the electrical power is on (TASK 24-22-00-860-811).

E. Operational Test of the Dedicated Battery System and Battery Pack for the Integrated

Standby Flight Display SUBTASK 34-24-02-210-006 (1) Do a check to see if the ISFD dedicated battery system (E4-1) and battery pack are serviceable: 34-24-02 (a) Make sure that the red FAULT light on the front of the battery charger is not on. NOTE: The red FAULT light shows that the battery charger or the battery pack are not serviceable. The battery charger or battery pack can be not serviceable because of problems with battery charger operating temperature, battery charger voltage output, or battery pack cell voltage. NOTE: If the red FAULT light is not on and a display shows on the integrated standby flight display, the battery charger and battery are serviceable. (b) Open circuit breaker on the front of the ISFD dedicated battery charger. (c) Close circuit breaker on the front of the ISFD dedicated battery charger. (d) Make sure that the yellow “ALT”, “SPD”, “ATT”, and “INIT XXs” flags are displayed on the ISFD for approximately 10 to 15 seconds after power up. NOTE: “XXs” refers to the time remaining (in seconds) for the ISFD to complete its initialization. Timer starts at 90s and counts down to 0s. (e) After 15 seconds, make sure that the display still show “ATT” and “INIT XXs” on the ISFD. (f) After 120 seconds, make sure that the display change to an attitude display. (g) Make sure that the BAT SW is in the ON position. (h) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name D 8 C01551 ISFD (i) Make sure that the ISFD display is not blank and continues to operate for 5-10 minutes. NOTE: A fully charged ISFD battery can operate for up to 150 minutes. (j) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name D 8 C01551 ISFD F . Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition SUBTASK 34-24-02-860-023 (1) If the electrical power is not necessary, turn the power supply off (TASK 24-22-00-860-812).

NOTE: This step tests the dedicated battery operation. The battery is replaced every three years for normal maintenance. NOTE: To restart the display initialization, push and release the ATT RST button on the face of the ISFD. NOTE: If the fault light is not on and a display shows on the integrated standby flight display, the battery charger is serviceable. (a) The red FAULT light comes on when there is a fault with the battery charger or the battery, from one or more of these conditions: 1) Battery charger operating temperature is more than the maximum 180°F (82°C) or less than the minimum 5°F (-15°C). 2) Battery charger circuits do not provide the correct output voltage. 3) Voltage levels of the cells in the battery pack are not equal. SUBTASK 34-31-00-710-001 (1) Do these steps to prepare for the operational test: (a) Set the VHF NAV switch on the instrument switching module to the NORMAL position. SUBTASK 34-31-31-420-001 (5) Install the localizer antenna [1] as follows: (a) Remove the protective covers from the electrical connectors [3]. (b) Apply sealant, A00247, to the threads of the screws [2]. (c) Connect the electrical connectors [3] to the localizer antenna [1]. (d) Align the localizer antenna [1] to the screw holes that hold the localizer antenna [1] to the airplane structure. (e) Install the screws [2] that attach the localizer antenna [1] to the airplane structure. (f) Tighten the screws [2] to 80 ±8 in-lb (9.0 ±0.9 N·m). SUBTASK 34-31-31-760-001 (6) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the localizer antenna [1] and airplane structure (SWPM 20-20-00). (a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. (b) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.001 ohms (1 milliohms) or less. SUBTASK 34-31-31-420-002 (7) Apply sealant, A00247, around the bases of the localizer antenna [1] to make a corrosion fillet seal (TASK 51-31-00-390-804). (a) Apply sealant, A00247, all around the edge of the localizer antenna [1]. (b) Use a sufficient quantity of sealant, A00247, to make the surface smooth. (c) Remove all the unwanted sealant, A00247, from the area around the antenna. (d) Let sealant, A00247, dry for the correct cure time. SUBTASK 34-31-31-410-001 (8) Close the nose radome (TASK 53-52-00-410-802). SUBTASK 34-31-31-860-006 (9) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2

(b) Set the SOURCE switch, on the instrument switching module, to the AUTO position. (c) Set the mode selector, on the captain's and the first officer's Electronic Flight Instrument System (EFIS) control panel, to the APP position. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-421 (d) Set a frequency of 108.1 MHz, on the captain's and the first officer's navigation control panels, as follows: 1) Turn the frequency selector until the frequency shows in the STANDBY window. 2) Push the TFR button. 3) Make sure that the frequency shows in the ACTIVE display. 422-999 (e) Set a ILS frequency of 108.10 MHz, on the captain's and the first officer's navigation control panels, as follows: 1) Push the MODE key (V or reverse V) until “ILS” is displayed in the STBY (lower) window of the Navigation Control Panel (NCP). 2) Push the number “108.10” with the NCP keypad. 3) Push the ACT/STBY transfer key until “ILS 108.10” is displayed in the ACT (upper) window, on the NCP . SUBTASK 34-31-31-860-007 (2) Put the NAV/COMM ramp test set, COM-1913, near the front of the airplane and a minimum of 6 ft (2 m) from the localizer antenna [1]. 34-31-42-700-801Part Number Check of the SoftwarePDF p. 527

2. Part Number Check of the Software

A. General

(1) This procedure gives instructions to check the part number (PN) of the software In MMR 1 and MMR 2 using headphones/speakers in the flight deck.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

C. Prepare for the checking of the Software PN

SUBTASK 34-31-42-860-016 (1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-31-42-700-003 (1) Do these steps to check the software PN: (a) Push, the NAV 1 knob (for MMR 1) or NAV2 knob (for MMR 2) on the captain’s or first officer (FO)’s Audio Control Panel to listen to MMR 1 or MMR 2. 34-31-42 1) Rotate, the NAV 1 knob (for MMR 1) or NAV2 knob (for MMR 2) on the captain’s or FO’s Audio Control Panel as necessary to adjust the volume to a desired level. (b) Set a ILS frequency of 108.10 MHz on the captain's or first officer's navigation control panel (NCP) by following one of these options: NOTE: The option is dependant on the airplane configuration. 1) Option 1: a) Push the MODE key (V or reverse V) until “ILS” is displayed in the STBY (lower) window of the NCP . b) Push the number “108.10” using the NCP keypad. c) Push the ACT/STBY transfer key until “ILS 108.10” is displayed in the ACT (upper) window on the NCP . 2) Option 2: a) Rotate the outer and inner knobs to dial the ILS frequency “108.10” in the right (STANDBY) window. b) Push the TFR key to move the frequency from the right (STANDBY) to the left (ACTIVE) window. 3) Push, the TEST button on the captain’s NCP to initiate a self-test of MMR 1 or on the FO’s NCP to initiate a self-test of MMR 2 4) Record, the installed software PN readout during the MMR 1 or MMR 2 self-test: • “MMR SYSTEM PART NUMBER XXXXXXXX-XXXX” (Not Required) • “SOFTWARE PART NUMBER XXXXX-XXXX-XXXX” (34 MMR OPS) • “CONFIGURATION PART NUMBER XXXXX-XXXX-XXXX” (34 MMR OSS) NOTE: Push the TEST button again, as necessary until all installed software PNs have been recorded. (c) If the software PNs are correct, then software installation is not needed. (d) If the software PNs are not correct, then install the software.

34-31-42-470-801Software Installation with a PDLPDF p. 528

3. Software Installation with a PDL

A. General

(1) This procedure gives instructions to install the Operational Program Software (OPS) and the operational configuration software (OSS) into the Multi-Mode Receiver (MMR) with a Portable Data Loader (PDL). Load the OPS software first, then load the OSS software. NOTE: The PDL must be connected to the MMR receiver through the RJ45 connector on the front of the receiver. When connected directly to the MMR front connector, an Ethernet cable is required. (2) A PDL is not a supplied part. Refer to the PDL supplier manual for instructions for operation. Some PDL have a disk drive for software installation from disks. If the PDL has an internal mass storage device, then disks are not necessary. 34-31-42 (3) Modern software loaders that meet the security requirements defined in ARINC 645-1 or newer are recommended to use. The procedures for modern software loaders will be marked as preferred for now and will be the only procedures available after removing floppy disk loaders procedures in the future. Please check with your Software Loader Supplier for current capabilities since this is still maturing across current and future software loaders. (4) For general information for software installation times and data loaders, do this task: On-Airplane Software - Installation, TASK 20-15-11-400-801.

B. Special Tools and Equipment

(1) Portable Data Loader: (2) Ethernet cable. (3) MMR OPSand MMR OSS software.

SUBTASK 34-31-42-820-001 (2) Do this task: Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the ISDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-802 or Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the FMC CDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-801. 34-31-42 SUBTASK 34-31-42-860-017 (3) Open the applicable circuit breaker and install a safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2 F . MMR NVM Download SUBTASK 34-31-42-970-001 (1) Download the MMR NVM data as follows: CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE CONNECTOR PINS, OR OTHER CONDUCTORS. IF YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENTS. (a) Remove the maintenance port access cover from the MMR. (b) Put the USB drive into the USB port on the MMR. (c) Remove the safety tag and close the applicable circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2 (d) Make sure that the top three lights flash yellow in a sequence from top to bottom. NOTE: This flash pattern shows that the NVM download is in progress. The pattern will change while the download continues but the lights will stay yellow. (e) Make sure that the top three lights flash green in the sequence that follows: NOTE: This flash pattern shows that the NVM download completed. This flash pattern will repeat with no end. It is safe to turn off the MMR and to remove the USB drive at this time. 1) In sequence from top to bottom. 2) All three lights at the same time. 3) Repeat. (f) Open the applicable circuit breaker and install a safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 34-31-42 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2 (g) Remove the USB drive from the USB port on the MMR. (h) Install the maintenance port access cover onto the MMR. (i) Remove the safety tag and close the applicable circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2 SUBTASK 34-31-42-970-002 (2) Convert the NVM data with the universal maintenance device, SPL-11321. (a) Put the USB drive into the USB port on the laptop. 1) Do not format the USB drive if prompted. (b) Open the USB Extract Tool application. (c) Select the USB drive when prompted. (d) Select Extract to... . (e) Enter the MMR serial number and NVM download date as the file name. (f) Select Save. NOTE: A file with the extension “.BIN” will be made. (g) Select OK to close the application. SUBTASK 34-31-42-470-005 (3) Send the .BIN file to Honeywell Aerotech Support and request for an Engineering Analysis.

34-32-11-000-802Marker Beacon Antenna with Gasket - RemovalPDF p. 576

3. Marker Beacon Antenna with Gasket - Removal (Figure 402)

A. General

(1) This procedure is used for the removal of antennas that use Aerobond or HI-TAK gaskets per 737–SL-20–045. NOTE: Reference the Aircraft Illustrated Parts Catalog for the gasket part number. (2) As a full certification test of the gasket was not done, it is recommended to do the steps that follow: (a) Do a visual inspection of the gasket and the mating surface, each a D check. (b) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion on the antenna and gasket after their removal. (c) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion and fretting caused by the antenna gasket. 1) Remove any corrosion and fretting on the airplane skin.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 100 Lower Half of Fuselage

C. Removal Procedure

SUBTASK 34-32-11-860-006 (1) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 1 C01374 RADIO NAVIGATION VOR/MKR BCN 1 SUBTASK 34-32-11-020-002 (2) Remove the marker beacon antenna [1]: (a) Remove the six bolts [2] from the antenna base. CAUTION MOVE THE ANTENNA ONLY AS FAR AS NECESSARY TO DISCONNECT CABLES. DAMAGE TO ANTENNA CABLES CAN OCCUR IF YOU PULL CABLES. (b) Lower the marker beacon antenna [1] until you can get access to the coaxial connector [3]. (c) Disconnect the coaxial connector [3] from the marker beacon antenna [1]. (d) Remove the marker beacon antenna [1]. (e) Remove and discard the gasket [4]. NOTE: For the Aerobond gasket, special attention must be used to remove the gel material residue to prevent silicone oil contamination on other parts of the airplane skin, which may cause paint adhesion difficulties.

Marker Beacon Antenna Installation SUBTASK 34-32-11-860-002 (1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open and has safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 1 C01374 RADIO NAVIGATION VOR/MKR BCN 1 SUBTASK 34-32-11-100-001 (2) Clean the airplane mating surface. WARNING DO NOT GET THE SOLVENT IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE IN THE FUMES FROM THE SOLVENT . PUT ON PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLES AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THE SOLVENT . KEEP THE SOLVENT AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THE SOLVENT IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE, WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (a) Clean the airplane mating surface with cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with Series 88 solvent, B01008 (TASK 20-30-88-910-801). (b) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, and clean the airplane mating surface again. (c) Do these two steps above until the airplane mating surface is clean and dry. SUBTASK 34-32-11-100-002 (3) If the airplane surface has corrosion or other damage, do these steps to prepare the airplane mating surface: (a) Remove the corrosion from the airplane mating surface, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Plated or Phosphated Surfaces, TASK 51-21-31-350-806. 34-32-11 (b) To apply a layer of coating, C00064, to the airplane mating surface, do this task: Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero, Bonderite M-CR ALCRM 1200 Aero, or Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero Application Process, TASK 51-21-41-370-802. SUBTASK 34-32-11-420-001 (4) Install the marker beacon antenna [1]. (a) Connect the coaxial connector [3] to the marker beacon antenna [1]. (b) Put the marker beacon antenna [1] in the correct position on the airplane surface. (c) Install five of the six bolts [2] in the base of the marker beacon antenna [1]. (d) Manually tighten the bolts [2] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). (e) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the baseplate of the marker beacon antenna [1] and airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). NOTE: Use the empty bolt hole to get access to the antenna baseplate. 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0025 ohms (2.5 milliohms) or less. (f) Install the last bolt [2]. 1) Manually tighten the bolt [2] to 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). SUBTASK 34-32-11-390-001 (5) Apply aerodynamic sealant. (a) Apply an aerodynamic fillet seal around the base of the marker beacon antenna [1] with sealant, A00247 (TASK 51-31-00-390-806 and TASK 20-30-11-910-801). NOTE: Operators can defer the application of the aero-sealant in the antenna installation until next “A” check or overnight maintenance stop to prevent a flight delay. The deferral of the application of sealant must not exceed a maximum of eight weeks (SL 20-043). (b) Use the hardwood or plastic fillet smoothing spatula, STD-810, to make a smooth 45-degree fillet. (c) Apply sealant, A00247, to the heads of the bolts [2] (TASK 51-31-00-390-806 and TASK 20-30-11-910-801). NOTE: Operators can defer the application of the aero-sealant in the antenna installation until next “A” check or overnight maintenance stop to prevent a flight delay. The deferral of the application of sealant must not exceed a maximum of eight weeks (SL 20-043). (d) Let the sealant dry for the correct cure time. (91 ±5 cm) below the marker beacon antenna. 3) Make sure that the test set faces to the nose landing gear. SUBTASK 34-32-11-860-007 (1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open and has safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 1 C01374 RADIO NAVIGATION VOR/MKR BCN 1 SUBTASK 34-32-11-100-003 (2) Clean the airplane mating surface: WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH, YOUR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE DANGEROUS MATERIALS. SOLVENTS CAN BE FLAMMABLE. OBEY THE MATERIAL SAFETY DATA SHEETS (MSDS) FOR SOLVENTS. (a) Clean the airplane mating surface with a cotton wiper, G00034, moistened with Series 88 solvent, B01008 (TASK 20-30-88-910-801). (b) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, and clean the airplane mating surface again. (c) Do these two steps above until the airplane mating surface is clean and dry. SUBTASK 34-32-11-420-002 (4) Install the marker beacon antenna [1]: (a) Remove the protective film from each side of the gasket [4]. NOTE: Reference the Aircraft Illustrated Parts Catalog for the gasket part number. (b) Put the gasket [4] on the marker beacon antenna. (c) Connect the coaxial connector [3] to the marker beacon antenna [1]. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY SEALANT TO THE EDGES OF THE ANTENNA. THE GASKET RELEASES THE MOISTURE. IF YOU SEAL THE EDGES, THE MOISTURE WILL STAY . THIS CAN CAUSE CORROSION DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE, AND ANTENNA MATING SURFACES. (d) Put the marker beacon antenna [1] in the correct position on the airplane surface. (e) Install five of the six bolts [2] in the base of the marker beacon antenna [1]. 34-32-11 1) Manually tighten the bolts [2] to 10 in-lb (1.13 N·m). NOTE: Since the gel material of the gasket is compressible, the bolts must be re-torqued 15 minutes after the installation to ensure tightness. 2) After 15 minutes, manually torque the bolts [2] to 16.5 ±1.5 in-lb (1.86 ±0.17 N·m). NOTE: To help prevent cracks, each antenna fastener could be tightened to a few pound-inches at a time until all fasteners are tightened. After a few minutes, each fastener can be tightened a few more pound-inches. This is repeated until each fastener is tightened to the recommended torque value. (f) Measure the resistance between the baseplate of the marker beacon antenna [1] and the airplane skin with an ohmmeter, STD-1045, or a intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550 NOTE: Use the empty bolt hole to get access to the antenna baseplate. 1) Make sure that the resistance is less than 2.5 milliohms. (g) Install the last bolt [2]. NOTE: Since the gel material of the gasket is compressible, the bolt must be re-torqued 15 minutes of the installation to ensure tightness. 2. Low Range Radio Altimeter System - Deactivation (Figure 201)

A. General

(1) This procedure removes electrical power to the LRRA System. NOTE: There are four LRRA antennas installed on the bottom of the airplane. The No. 1 (M1737) and No. 2 (M1738) transmit antennas are the outer antennas. The No. 1 (M1739) and the No. 2 (M1740) receive antennas are the inner antennas.

(e) Touch the light gray bar to open the Launch Bar. (f) Touch Test Setup to show the Test Setup window. NOTE: This window is used to configure the test set operational parameters. (g) Touch the light gray bar to close the Launch Bar. (h) Make sure that these RF Port Settings, UUT Settings, and RF Settings are correct on the General tab: 1) Connection Type - Coupler 2) UUT Detect Mode - Auto 3) Level Mode - Auto. (i) Make sure that these RF Port Settings and RF Settings are correct on the Loss tab: 34-33-00 1) TX Cable Loss - See cable for value in dBs 2) RX Cable Loss - See cable for value in dBs 3) TX Coupler Loss - See TX Antenna Coupler for value in dBs 4) RX Coupler Loss - See RX Antenna Coupler for value in dBs. (j) Touch Delay Calibration to show the Delay Calibration screen. NOTE: This screen starts the calibration procedure for the test set RF coaxial cable delay. 1) Connect the ends of the TX and RX cables together with the supplied TNC connector. 2) Touch Start to start delay calibration. NOTE: Delay calibration can not be aborted once started. The calibration process is automatic and the Test Setup screen is shown when calibration is completed. 3) Disconnect the TNC connector from the TX and RX cables. You do not see any TX power from the UUT and the test would not work. (a) Select and assemble the sectional pole lengths to support the antenna couplers. (b) Mount the antenna coupler to the end of each assembled pole. (c) Push down on each pole assembly until the gas shock compresses and locks the retaining clamp. (d) Raise the TX pole assembly and place the antenna coupler over the applicable radio altimeter transmit antenna. 1) If the pole is vertical, release the gas shock retaining clamp to apply upward pressure on the antenna coupler. (e) Raise the RX pole assembly and place the antenna coupler over the applicable radio altimeter receive antenna. 1) When the pole is vertical, release the gas shock retaining clamp to apply upward pressure on the antenna coupler. (f) Connect the TX and RX coax cables to the TX and RX antenna couplers TNC connector. H. Radio Altitude Simulation Test (Using the Atlantis DRA707 Test Set)

SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-015 (1) Prepare the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922, for the altitude simulation, do these steps: (a) Set the power ON/OFF switch to the ON position. 1) Make sure that the 5 VDC and HOLDING lights come on. (b) Set the NO COMPUTED DATA switches to the NORMAL position. (c) Push and release the PRES ALT key. 1) Make sure that PRES ALT shows on the Light Emitting Diode (LED)s. (d) Use the keypad to put in a value of +4000 feet. (e) Push and release the ENTER key. 1) Make sure that the radio altitude value shown on the EFIS displays is blank. SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-016 (2) Prepare the captain's and the first officer's EFIS control panels for the simulation. (a) Push and release the RST (reset) button. (b) Turn the DH control to show DH 450 at the captain's EFIS display. (c) Turn the DH control to show DH 400 at the first officer's EFIS display. SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-017 (3) Set these controls on the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922: (a) Push and release the START ALT key. 1) Make sure that START ALT shown on the LEDs. (b) Use the keypad to put in a value of +4000 feet. (c) Push and release the ENTER key. 1) Make sure that the LEDs show START ALT +4000. (d) Push and release the STOP ALT key. 1) Make sure that the LEDs show STOP ALT . (e) Use the keypad to put in a value of -20 feet. (f) Push and release the ENTER key. 1) Make sure that the LEDs show STOP ALT -20. (g) Push and release the VERT SPD key. 1) Make sure that the LEDs show VERT SPD. (h) Use the keypad to put in a value of -4000 (feet per minute). (i) Push and release the ENTER key. 1) Make sure that the LEDs show VERT SPD -4000. SUBTASK 34-33-00-730-009 (4) Do the altitude ramp-down test (typical). (a) Push the RAMP/HOLD key on the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922. 1) Make sure that the RAMPING light comes on. (b) Look for these indications on the captain's and the first officer's EFIS displays. 1) The radio altitude goes out of view for approximately 22.5 seconds while the altitude on the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922, decreases from 4000 to 2500 feet. 34-33-00 (c) After the time-out of 22.5 seconds (previous step), a radio altitude of 2500 feet comes into view on the EFIS displays and decreases toward zero. NOTE: The EFIS displays show the radio altitude set on the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922, within the limit of 2500 feet to -20 feet. (d) Look for these indications on the captain's EFIS display when the radio altitude decreases to 450 feet: 1) The DH value changes to a yellow color and flashes for 3 seconds. 2) The radio altitude continues to decrease toward zero. (e) Look for these indications on the first officer's EFIS display when the radio altitude decreases to 400 feet: 1) The DH value changes to a yellow color and flashes for 3 seconds. 2) The DH value flashes for approximately 3 seconds. 3) The radio altitude continues to decrease toward zero. (f) Look for these indications on the EFIS displays while the radio altitude decreases to zero feet: 1) The radio altitude value changes to a white color. 2) The DH value changes to the numbers set at the captain's and the first officer's EFIS control panels.

I. Radio Altitude Simulation Test (Using Aeroflex ALT-8000 Test Set) (Alternate)

SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-032 (1) Prepare the Aeroflex ALT-8000 test set (radio altimeter test set, COM-14227), for the altitude simulation: (a) Touch Alt. Ind. Zero to show the Altitude Indicator Zero screen. NOTE: The test set is now simulating 0 ft (0 m) at the end of the ALT-8000 RF coax cables. SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-033 (2) Prepare the captain's and the first officer's EFIS control panels for the simulation. (a) Push and release the RST (reset) button. (b) Turn the DH control to show DH 450 at the captain's EFIS display. (c) Turn the DH control to show DH 400 at the first officer's EFIS display. SUBTASK 34-33-00-730-012 (3) Do the altitude ramp-down test: (a) Touch the light gray bar to open the Launch Bar. (b) Touch Simulation window to show the Simulation window. NOTE: The Simulation window is the main test screen and provides visual access to control parameters and test data. (c) Touch the light gray bar to close the Launch Bar. (d) Set these values in the Control area of the Simulation window: NOTE: When a numeric data field is touched for editing, a data entry pop-up window is shown. A numeric keypad, data slew bar or rotary knob pop-up window can be used to enter a value. 1) Start Altitude = 3000 ft (914.4 m) 34-33-00 2) Stop Altitude = 0 ft (0 m) 3) Altitude Rate = 100 ft/min (0.508 m/s). NOTE: DH trips should be completed with an altitude ramp-down and descent rate of 100 ft/min or less, to let the DH indicator and any audible warning operate correctly. (e) Touch Run to start simulation. NOTE: Altitude Pause is shown. NOTE: To pause simulation at any point, touch Altitude Pause. The Current Altitude can be changed and the simulation is started again with a touch of Altitude Resume. 1) The test set Current Altitude shows 3000 ft (914.4 m) and starts to decrease toward 0 ft (0 m). (f) Make sure that the captain's and first officers EFIS display show these values: 1) No radio altitude shows until the Current Altitude reaches 2500 ft (762.0 m). 2) When the Current Altitude reaches 450 ft (137.2 m), the decision height indications on the captain's EFIS display change. 3) When the Current Altitude reaches 400 ft (121.9 m), the decision height indications on the first officers EFIS display change. 4) The Current Altitude on the test set and the radio altitude on the EFIS display continue to decrease to 0 ft (0 m). (g) Touch Stop to end the simulation. SUBTASK 34-33-00-710-010 (4) If it is necessary, use the test set to do altitude simulations to test other airplane systems.

34-33-00-710-801Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) System - Operational TestPDF p. 601

2. Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) System - Operational Test

A. General

(1) The operational test includes a LRRA Interface To Display Electronic Unit test. (2) The operational test makes sure the interface between the transceiver and the displays is ok. (3) The operational test does not include a check of the LRRA antennas. (4) This test will make sure the that the radio altimeter operates correctly after a suspected 5G interference. (a) There can be 5G interference to the radio altimeter signals because of the frequency spectrum (3.4 GHz - 4.2 GHz, 4.4 GHz - 4.9 GHz), antenna type, and power levels used by the 5G technology. The radio altimeters can become inoperative or can supply erroneous data, which can affect other systems on the airplane that use radio altimeter data. 1) Follow your airline policy for reporting the specific event. 2) For more information refer to 737NG-FTD-34-21001.

34-33-00-730-801Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) System - System TestPDF p. 602

3. Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) System - System Test

A. General

(1) The system test makes sure that the interface between the Air/Ground relays is ok and the transmit and receive antennas operate correctly. (2) The system test includes these tests: (a) The LRRA Air/Ground Discrete Input Test (b) The LRRA Antenna Coaxial Cable Test. 1) Interface from LRRA equipment rack connector to antenna connector. 2) Interface from LRRA R/T to antenna connector. (3) For airplanes with predictive wind shear weather radar systems, open the Weather Radar (WXR) transceiver circuit breaker to make sure that the WXR system does not come on. The radio altimeter supplies radio altitude data to the WXR transceiver. The WXR transceiver uses the radio altitude data to turn the WXR system on and off.

E. Air/Ground Discrete Input Test

SUBTASK 34-33-00-860-005 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name B 4 C01384 RADIO NAVIGATION RADIO ALTM 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 16 C01385 RADIO NAVIGATION RADIO ALTM 2 34-33-00 (Continued) F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 13 C00120 WEATHER RADAR RT SUBTASK 34-33-00-020-001 (2) Remove the No. 1 and the No. 2 LRRA R/T s (TASK 34-33-21-000-801). SUBTASK 34-33-00-730-001 (3) Use a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, to measure the resistance between the AIR/GROUND DISCRETE, pin F4, and the IND 2 STATUS, pin F6, in connector D3667B for the No. 1 radio altimeter system. (a) Make sure that the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, shows 10 KOhms or more than 10 KOhms. SUBTASK 34-33-00-730-002 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF ALL CONTROL SURFACES BEFORE YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. AILERONS, RUDDERS, ELEVATORS, FLAPS, SPOILERS AND THE THRUST REVERSERS CAN MOVE QUICKLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (4) On the Proximity Switch Electronics Unit (PSEU), push the ON/OFF button to turn the BITE display to ON. (a) Push the NO button for the “EXISTING FAULTS ?” display. (b) Push the NO button for the “FAULT HISTORY ?” display. (c) Push the NO button for the “GROUND TEST ?” display. (d) Push the YES button for the “AIR/GROUND OVRD ?” display. 34-33-11-000-803Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Removal with GasketPDF p. 613

3. Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Removal with Gasket (Figure 402)

A. General

(1) This task includes the steps to remove the Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) antenna. (2) The LRRA antenna can be removed by one of these two methods: • Inside the fuselage • Outside the fuselage. (a) The application of the self-leveling sealant and connector compound can prevent removal of the antenna from outside the fuselage. (3) Imprints on the fuselage skin caused by the gasket wire mesh are permitted. If such imprints are found, then no maintenance action is necessary.

34-33-11-400-803Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Installation with GasketPDF p. 622

5. Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Installation with Gasket (Figure 402)

A. General

(1) This task includes the steps to install the Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) antenna. (2) The LRRA antenna can be installed by one of these two methods: • Inside the fuselage • Outside the fuselage. (a) The antenna must be installed from inside the fuselage if the self-leveling sealant and connector compound will be applied. This method makes sure that sufficient access is allowed for the correct installation of the sealant and compound. (b) If the self-leveling sealant and connector compound will be deferred, then the antenna can be installed from outside the fuselage.

D. Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Inspection

SUBTASK 34-33-11-200-001 (1) Examine the outer surface of the antenna for a circular area ¼ in. (6.35 mm) or larger that is not constant and smooth. (a) If an area is found, replace the antenna, do these tasks: • Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Removal with O-Ring, TASK 34-33-11-000-801 or Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Removal with Gasket, TASK 34-33-11-000-803 • Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Installation with O-Ring, TASK 34-33-11-400-801 or Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Installation with Gasket, TASK 34-33-11-400-803. 34-33-11 SUBTASK 34-33-11-020-001 (2) Remove the radio altimeter antenna, do this task: Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Removal with O-Ring, TASK 34-33-11-000-801 or Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Removal with Gasket, TASK 34-33-11-000-803. NOTE: The antenna connector is inspected and cleaned during the connector removal. SUBTASK 34-33-11-120-001 (3) Remove all unwanted material from around the connector and backplate. SUBTASK 34-33-11-210-001 (4) This subtask is only for the airplanes with Radio Altimeter antenna P/N DMPN19-1-1 installed: NOTE: Ignore this Subtask if there is no Radio Altimeter antenna P/N DMPN19-1-1 installed on the airplane. (a) Examine the four nuts on the electrical connector for corrosion. 1) If a nut is not there or loose, or has corrosion, replace the antenna (TASK 34-33-11-000-801 or TASK 34-33-11-000-803 and TASK 34-33-11-400-801 or TASK 34-33-11-400-803). NOTE: Do not replace nuts that have corrosion. This will change the correct operation of the antenna. (b) Examine the antenna connector and backplate for corrosion. NOTE: If there is corrosion on the surface in the inner diameter of the O-ring seal, but the connector nuts have no corrosion, do not replace the antenna. It will operate correctly. SUBTASK 34-33-11-120-002 (5) Clean the backplate and connector where there is corrosion on the surface. WARNING ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IS TOXIC AND FLAMMABLE. USE PERSONAL PROTECTION EQUIPMENT . USE IN A WELL-VENTILATED AREA. (a) Use alcohol, B50073. NOTE: Avoid the use of excessive alcohol. (b) Remove excessive alcohol, B50073, by wiping with a clean dry cotton wiper, G00034. SUBTASK 34-33-11-420-006 (6) Install the antenna, do this task: Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Installation with O-Ring, TASK 34-33-11-400-801 or Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) Antenna Installation with Gasket, TASK 34-33-11-400-803.

2. Weather Radar (WXR) System - Deactivation (Figure 201)

A. General

CAUTION WHEN YOU OPERATE THE WEATHER RADAR FOR NON-TEST MODES, POINT THE NOSE OF THE AIRPLANE WHERE IT IS FREE OF LARGE METAL OBJECTS. KEEP THE FORWARD 180-DEGREE AREA CLEAR. THIS INCLUDES HANGARS, TRUCKS, OTHER AIRPLANES. THIS 300 FEET DISTANCE MUST BE CLEAR OR DAMAGE TO THE RECEIVER CAN OCCUR. (1) This procedure removes electrical power to the Weather Radar system.

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-858 Tag - DO NOT OPERATE

C. Location Zones

THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT IN THE AREA OF THE NOSE RADOME. (1) Attach a DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858 to the thrust levers. SUBTASK 34-43-00-860-264 (2) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 13 C00120 WEATHER RADAR RT

3. Weather Radar (WXR) System - Activation (Figure 201)

A. General

CAUTION WHEN YOU OPERATE THE WEATHER RADAR FOR NON-TEST MODES, POINT THE NOSE OF THE AIRPLANE WHERE IT IS FREE OF LARGE METAL OBJECTS. KEEP THE FORWARD 180-DEGREE AREA CLEAR. THIS INCLUDES HANGARS, TRUCKS, OTHER AIRPLANES. THIS 300 FEET DISTANCE MUST BE CLEAR OR DAMAGE TO THE RECEIVER CAN OCCUR. (1) This procedure adds electrical power to the Weather Radar system.

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-858 Tag - DO NOT OPERATE

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 111 Radome 112 Area Forward of Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-43-00-860-268 WARNING DO NOT OPERATE THE WEATHER RADAR WITHIN 3.3 FEET (1 METER) OF REFUELING OR DE-FUELING OPERATIONS, A FUEL SPILL OR OPEN FUEL CELLS. OPERATION OF THE WEATHER RADAR WITHIN THE 3.3 FEET (1 METER) LIMIT CAN CAUSE A FIRE OR EXPLOSION. A FIRE OR EXPLOSION CAN CAUSE INJURY OR DEATH TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . WARNING DO NOT OPEN THE NOSE RADOME IF THE WIND IS MORE THAN 15 KNOTS. IF YOU OPEN THE NOSE RADOME IN A WIND, THE RADOME CAN MOVE QUICKLY . THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . WARNING DO NOT OPERATE THE WEATHER RADAR WHEN PERSONNEL ARE IN THE AREA USUALLY ENCLOSED BY THE AIRCRAFT NOSE RADOME OR IN A HANGAR. THESE CONDITIONS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONNEL. NOTE: The hangar restriction DOES NOT apply to the weather radar test mode. (1) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 13 C00120 WEATHER RADAR RT SUBTASK 34-43-00-860-269 (2) Do the following steps at the WXR control panel: 34-43-00 (a) Set mode select /power switch (as applicable) to the ON position. (b) Push the TEST/TEST MODE switch on the control panel. 1) Make sure aural warnings are heard. SUBTASK 34-43-00-010-001 (3) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858 from the thrust levers.

34-43-11-400-802Weather Radar Antenna Drive Unit InstallationPDF p. 689

5. Weather Radar Antenna Drive Unit Installation (Figure 402)

A. General

(1) This task has the steps to install the weather radar antenna drive unit. 349-999 (2) An auto alignment process will take place and will require up to 30 minutes to complete depending on the flight profile. NOTE: No matter which procedure is done to more quickly auto align the system, the weather radar system will continue to do its function correctly. But, initially (until auto-alignment process completes on its own) there could be decreased long range weather detection (if antenna aims too high) or unwanted ground clutter shown (if antenna aims too low). (a) Recommended flight profile for auto-alignment: 1) Achieve cruise altitude at minimum 17000 feet above prevailing terrain in radar field of view. 2) System is in the Auto mode. NOTE: Switching to the manual mode will interrupt WXR auto-alignment. 3) Un-accelerated straight level flight, no maneuvering. 4) Not over mountainous terrain or large variations of terrain. NOTE: The automatic alignment feature will work in mountainous terrain. But, it could take longer to complete. 5) Not in visible weather, no significant weather within the radar field of view between 80 nmi (148 km) and 140 nmi (259 km). 6) Not over water. NOTE: Flying over water could give weak returns. ALL

34-43-11-200-801Weather Radar Antenna Flat Plate InspectionPDF p. 695

2. Weather Radar Antenna Flat Plate Inspection

A. General

(1) The purpose of this task is to examine the antenna flat plate for wear to make sure that it is in a serviceable condition. Types of wear include: (a) Corrosion (b) Dents (c) Holes, gouges and tears (d) Warping (e) Foreign objects (f) Lightning strikes. 349-999 (2) The antenna flat plate is divided into three zones. This is to help easily identify wear: (a) Zone 2 is the area outside a 10.5 in. (266.7 mm) radius from the center. (b) Zone 3 is the area inside a 10.5 in. (266.7 mm) radius from the center. (c) Zone 4 is the feed waveguide. (3) A single radiating waveguide is defined as one of the channels that run parallel between the two surfaces of the antenna flat plate. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-348 (4) The antenna flat plate is divided into four zones. This is to help easily identify wear: (a) Zone 1 is the outer edges outside the waveguide terminal zone or waveguide end plates. (b) Zone 2 is the area outside a 10.5 in. (266.7 mm) radius from the center. (c) Zone 3 is the area inside a 10.5 in. (266.7 mm) radius from the center. (d) Zone 4 is the feed waveguide. (5) A single radiating waveguide is defined as one of the channels that run parallel between the two surfaces of the antenna flat plate. ALL (6) If it is necessary to replace the antenna flat plate, refer to Weather Radar Antenna Flat Plate Removal, TASK 34-43-11-000-801 and Weather Radar Antenna Flat Plate Installation, TASK 34-43-11-400-801.

H. Weather Radar Antenna Flat Plate Inspection

(Figure 602) NOTE: Dents are defined as damage that could have occurred because of the surface being hit by a blow or crushed by a point load. NOTE: The manufacturing procedure can cause an antenna flat plate that shows a small quantity of generalized warping or slow changes in the flat of the surface. The general warping/change must not be regarded as a dent if it occurs on an area of 2.5 ±0.5 in. (63.5 ±12.7 mm). SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-010 WARNING YOU MUST WEAR GOGGLES OR A FACE SHIELD WHEN YOU USE THE EXTERNAL ABRASIVE BLASTING EQUIPMENT . IF YOU DO NOT USE THE PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT , INJURIES CAN OCCUR. (1) Examine the antenna flat plate, the flat plate slots, waveguide and interior for corrosion: (a) If corrosion is found in the slots, then the antenna flat plate must be replaced. (b) If corrosion is found, remove as follows: 1) Blow off loose material from the two sides of the antenna flat plate with an air supply, STD-6852. 2) Remove loose material on the two sides of the antenna flat plate with an emery cloth, STD-6449. 3) Clean the front and rear of the antenna flat plate with alcohol, B00130. 4) Apply coating, C50395 to exposed or bare metal areas on the front or rear surfaces. SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-026 (2) Examine the antenna flat plate for etching, nicks, pits or scratches (front and rear): (a) An antenna flat plate is unservicable if the etching, nicks, pits, or scratches on the front surface: 1) Are not caused by the manufacturing process (i.e., brazing, cleaning, honing, tool no larger than 0.030 in. (0.8 mm), etc.) or not the reasonable consequence of valid handling procedures and are not collectively limited to less than 25% of the surface area. SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-011 (3) Examine the antenna flat plate for dents in zone 2 (front and rear): (a) Dents must be 0.05 in. (1.27 mm) or less in depth. (b) A maximum of two dents on a single radiating waveguide. (c) A maximum of seven dents in zone 2 in total. SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-012 (4) Examine the antenna flat plate for dents in zone 3 (front and rear): (a) Dents must be 0.03 in. (0.76 mm) or less in depth. (b) A maximum of one dent on a single radiating waveguide. (c) A maximum of three dents in zone 3 in total. SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-014 (5) Examine the antenna flat plate for dents in zone 4 (front and rear): (a) No dents are permitted in the feed waveguide (zone 4). 34-43-11 349-999 (Continued) SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-015 (6) Examine the antenna flat plate (front and rear): (a) No damage is permitted to the partitions or end plates related to a single radiating waveguide in which a surface dent has also occurred. (b) If the front or rear surfaces show through the surface holes (other than slots), or have breaks or cracks, the unit must be replaced. SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-017 (7) Examine the slots on the front and rear of the antenna flat plate: (a) Dents that cause damage to the surface slots will make the antenna flat plate unserviceable. (b) The surface slot must not show localized dents or signs of mechanical rework, such as file marks or rough edges. SUBTASK 34-43-11-210-018 (8) Examine the antenna flat plate outer edge (the outer 1 in. (25 mm), front and rear) for small dents, bending, marks and handling damage: (a) These are permitted if they agree with the following criteria: NOTE: If the anomalies do not agree with the criteria below then the antenna flat plate is unserviceable. 1) Does not structurally impair the antenna. 2) Does not exceed more than 25% of the circumference of either the front or rear surface. 3) Does not occur in large numbers on a new production antenna such that the antenna appears not to be new. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-348

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-43-21-860-002 (1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is open and has safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 13 C00120 WEATHER RADAR RT 34-43-21 F . Waveguide Assembly [1] Installation SUBTASK 34-43-21-860-003 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU CLOSE THE NOSE RADOME WHEN IT RAINS. IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT OPEN THE NOSE RADOME IF THE WIND IS MORE THAN 15 KNOTS. IF YOU OPEN THE NOSE RADOME IN A WIND, THE RADOME CAN MOVE QUICKLY . THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (1) Make sure the nose radome is open. SUBTASK 34-43-21-420-001 CAUTION DO NOT LET THE WORKSTANDS HIT OR TOUCH THE WEATHER RADAR ANTENNA OR OTHER RADOME EQUIPMENT . IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (2) Install waveguide assembly [1]: (a) Remove the dust caps from the ends of the waveguides. (b) Examine the waveguide assembly [1] for damage, dirt, and moisture. NOTE: The clear plastic window in the antenna waveguide is to keep dirt, moisture, or other contaminants from entering the waveguide. It is not mandatory to replace the clear plastic window if it has been removed, however it is recommended. (c) Install a new gasket [10] on the pressure seal flange [9]. (d) Install a new gasket [14] at one end of waveguide assembly [1]. (e) Move waveguide assembly [1] through the hole in the forward bulkhead and put in the correct position. 1) Make sure that gasket [10] and gasket [14] are correctly installed. (f) Install screws [7] and screw [8] to hold the pressure seal flange [9] to the bulkhead. 1) Make sure that longer screw [8] is installed in the correct location. (g) Install the quick-disconnect [2] that holds waveguide assembly [1] to the antenna drive unit with new gasket [20] between. (h) Install the waveguide clamp [3], screw [4], washer [5], and nut [6]. 1) Adjust the clamp to make sure it does not bend waveguide assembly [1]. (i) If you did not remove waveguide assembly [11], then do this step: 1) Install the screws [12] and washers [13] that attach waveguide assembly [1] to waveguide assembly [11].

G. Waveguide Assembly [11] Installation

SUBTASK 34-43-21-420-002 (1) Install waveguide assembly [11]: (a) Remove the dust caps from the ends of the waveguides. 34-43-21 (b) Examine the waveguide assembly [11] for damage, dirt and moisture. NOTE: The clear plastic window in the antenna waveguide is to keep dirt, moisture, or other contaminants from entering the waveguide. It is not mandatory to replace the clear plastic window if it has been removed, however it is recommended. (c) Make sure that a new gasket [14] is installed at each end of waveguide assembly [11]. (d) Install the screws [12] and washers [13] that attach waveguide assembly [11] to the mount waveguide. (e) Install the screws [12] and washers [13] that attach waveguide assembly [11] to waveguide assembly [1]. SUBTASK 34-43-21-410-005 (2) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 111 Radome (a) Install the screws that attach the nose radome to the fuselage bulkhead SUBTASK 34-43-21-420-003 (3) If you removed the WXR receiver/transmitter, then, do this task: Weather Radar Receiver/Transmitter Installation, TASK 34-43-41-400-801. NOTE: A force of approximately 10 pounds is necessary to overcome the retainer springs. The handle on the front of the receiver/transmitter is used to pull the unit down to overcome the retainer springs. 34-45-00-970-801Flight History Data DownloadPDF p. 757

2. Flight History Data Download

A. General

(1) This procedure allows a complete listing of stored fault history information, and Traffic Advisory (TA)/Resolution Advisory (RA) events to be downloaded from the TPA-100 Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) processor onto a portable Personal Computer Memory Card Interface Adapter (PCMCIA) flash card. (2) A blank Personal Computer (PC) Air Transport Association (ATA) card with memory capability up to 512 megabytes, or a Compact Flash (CF) using an adapter may be used for the download procedures.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left 118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-45-00-869-001 (1) Make sure power to the TCAS Processor is turned off. (a) Open this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name B 6 C01195 TCAS SUBTASK 34-45-00-869-002 (2) On the TCAS Processor, open the front panel access cover. SUBTASK 34-45-00-869-003 (3) Insert a blank PC ATA card into the PCMCIA slot. 34-45-00 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 006, 007, 018, 019 POST SB 737-34-2403; 013, 014 POST SB 737-34-2938 (Continued) SUBTASK 34-45-00-869-004 (4) Close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name B 6 C01195 TCAS SUBTASK 34-45-00-869-005 (5) Verify that there is a blinking red light in the PCMCIA slot. SUBTASK 34-45-00-869-006 (6) Verify that the following message displays on the Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) display on the front of the TCAS Processor. (a) CARD INSERTED (b) DUMP REQUEST (c) > GO BACK NOTE: This message will stay on the screen for approximately five minutes. SUBTASK 34-45-00-869-007 (7) Verify that the following message displays on the LCD display on the front of the TCAS Processor when the data dump is complete. (a) CARD INSERTED (b) DUMP COMPLETE (c) > GO BACK SUBTASK 34-45-00-869-008 (8) Remove the PC ATA card from the TCAS Processor. SUBTASK 34-45-00-869-009 (9) Close the access cover. SUBTASK 34-45-00-869-010 (10) Restore the airplane to the usual condition ALL

34-45-00-710-801TCAS - Operational TestPDF p. 779

2. TCAS - Operational Test

A. General

(1) This test makes sure the Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) operates correctly. It uses only the system's Built-In-Test Equipment (BITE) functions. Special test or ground equipment is not necessary.

B. References

Reference Title 23-51-00-710-801 Flight Interphone System - Operational Test (P/B 501) 31-62-00-710-801 Common Display System - Operational Test (P/B 501) 34-21-00-710-801 Air Data Inertial Reference System - Operational Test (P/B 501) 34-21-00-820-801 Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the FMC CDU (P/B 201) 34-21-00-820-802 Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the ISDU (P/B 201) 34-33-00-710-801 Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) System - Operational Test (P/B 501) 34-53-00-710-801 Air Traffic Control System - Operational Test (P/B 501)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left 118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Prepare for the Operational Test

SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-002 (1) Make sure these systems are serviceable: (a) Air Data System (TASK 34-21-00-710-801). (b) Air Traffic Control (ATC) System (TASK 34-53-00-710-801). (c) Common Display System (CDS) (TASK 31-62-00-710-801). (d) Flight Interphone System (FIS) (TASK 23-51-00-710-801). (e) Low Range Radio Altimeter (LRRA) System (TASK 34-33-00-710-801). 34-45-00 SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-003 (2) Do this task: Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the ISDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-802 or Air Data Inertial Reference System - Alignment from the FMC CDU, TASK 34-21-00-820-801. SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-034 (3) Wait until the align light on the Mode Select Unit (MSU) goes off. SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-004 (4) Put the display mode switch on the Electronic Flight Instrument System (EFIS) control panel to the MAP position. SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-035 (5) Put the range knob on the EFIS control panel to 10. SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-005 (6) Put the mode select switch on the ATC control panel to the TA/RA position. SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-006 (7) Push the TFC switch on the EFIS control panel. (a) Make sure the inboard display shows TFC. SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-007 (8) Put the transponder select switch on the ATC control panel to the 1 position. (a) Make sure the FAIL lamp on the ATC control panel is off. SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-008 (9) Put the mode select switch on the ATC control panel to the STBY position. (a) Make sure the inboard displays show the TCAS OFF indication. (b) Put the mode reply switch on the ATC control panel to the ON position. SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-009 (10) Put the mode select switch on the ATC control panel to the TA position. (a) Make sure the inboard displays show the TA ONLY indication. SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-010 (11) Put the mode select switch on the ATC control panel to the TA/RA position. (a) Make sure TA ONLY continues to show on the inboard displays. SUBTASK 34-45-00-860-078 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE ATC TRANSPONDERS ARE IN THE STANDBY MODE WHEN YOU SIMULATE ALTITUDE. YOU CAN ACCIDENTALLY CAUSE TCAS TARGETS. AIR TRAFFIC IN THE AREA WILL CHANGE DIRECTION QUICKLY TO GO AWAY FROM THESE TARGETS. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (12) Make sure that the ATC transponders are in standby mode. (a) Put the mode select switch on the ATC control panel to the STBY position.

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-45-00-740-001 (1) Do the operational test as follows: (a) Turn and release the mode select switch on the ATC control panel to the TEST position and hold it for one second. 34-45-00 (b) Make sure these results occur: 1) The inboard displays show a test pattern as described below (Figure 501): a) TCAS TEST shows on the left side of the inboard displays b) The word TRAFFIC shows on the right side of the inboard displays 043, 044 c) An R/A (red square) shows at 3 o'clock and flying level (no arrow). 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 d) An R/A (red square) shows at 3 o'clock and flying level (no arrow). ALL e) A Traffic Advisory (yellow circle) shows at 9 o'clock and climbing (up arrow). 043, 044 f) Proximity Traffic (solid white diamond) shows at 1 o'clock and descending (down arrow). 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 g) Proximity Traffic (solid white diamond) shows at 1 o'clock and descending (down arrow). ALL h) Non-Threat Traffic (open white diamond) shows at 11 o'clock and flying level (no arrow). 2) Make sure the outboard displays show the DO NOT CLIMB and DO NOT DESCEND resolution advisory. 3) A TCAS SYSTEM TEST OK synthesized voice announcement comes on at the end of the test if the test passes. SUBTASK 34-45-00-740-002 (2) Do the operational test again with the transponder select switch on the ATC control panel set to the 2 position. SUBTASK 34-45-00-840-005 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THE ATC TRANSPONDERS ARE IN THE STANDBY MODE WHEN YOU SIMULATE ALTITUDE. YOU CAN ACCIDENTALLY CAUSE TCAS TARGETS. AIR TRAFFIC IN THE AREA WILL CHANGE DIRECTION QUICKLY TO GO AWAY FROM THESE TARGETS. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (3) Make sure that the ATC transponders are in standby mode. (a) Put the mode select switch on the ATC control panel to the STBY position.

34-45-00-730-801TCAS - System Test (With the IFR TCAS-201 Test Set)PDF p. 784

3. TCAS - System Test (With the IFR TCAS-201 Test Set)

A. General

(1) This test is a complete system test of the Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS). The system test first runs the Operational Test, and then does a test of the TCAS with ground test equipment.
