(e) Do a check of the Mode S Address. 1) Set the AUTO/TEST/MANUAL switch to the MANUAL position until Mode S Address screen shows. 2) Make sure that the Mode S Address field shows the correct Mode S Address. Refer to (WDM 34-53-11, 34-53-21) for the Mode S Address code. (f) Do a check of the Airborne Surveillance Status. 1) Notify local ATC facilities that transponder testing of the Surveillance Status will be performed. 2) Set the AUTO/TEST/MANUAL switch to the MANUAL position until the Airborne Surveillance Status screen shows. 3) On the ATC control panel, change the code switches to a different ATC ID code. 4) Make sure that the SURV STAT field changes to TEMP ALERT . 5) Set code switches on the ATC control panel back to the original code. 6) Push the IDENT switch on the ATC Control Panel. 7) Make sure that the SURV STAT field shows SPI. (g) Do a check of the Airborne Position Quality Indicator. 1) Set the AUTO/TEST/MANUAL switch to the MANUAL position until the Position Hex screen shows. 2) Make sure that the TYP field does not show 0 or 18. NOTE: If TYPE shows 0 the transponder does not receive position data from the IRS or Multimode Receiver (MMR). A TYPE of 18 indicates the transponder receives position data but not from the MMR. 417-446, 500-999 (h) Do a check of the Type 28 Decoded. 1) Set the AUTO/TEST/MANUAL switch to the MANUAL position until the Type 28 Decoded screen shows. 2) Make sure that NO EMERGENCY is displayed. (i) Do a check of the Horizontal Position Integrity. 34-53-00 417-446, 500-999 (Continued) 1) Set the AUTO/TEST/MANUAL switch to the MANUAL position until the Horizontal Position Integrity screen shows. 2) Make sure that the DO260B shows in the HZ POS field. 3) Make sure that the display shows SIL = 3. 4) Make sure that the display shows NACp = 8 or a value more than 8. 5) Make sure that the display shows NIC = 7 or a value more than 7. (j) Do a check of the Airborne Velocity Accuracy and System Design Accuracy. 1) Set the AUTO/TEST/MANUAL switch to the MANUAL position until the Air Vel Acc and the Sys Des Acc screen shows. 2) Make sure that the display shows NACv = 1 or NACv = 2. 3) Make sure that the display shows SDA = 2. (k) Do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802 (l) Do a check of the Airplane Length/Width. 1) Set the AUTO/TEST/MANUAL switch to the MANUAL position until the Length/Width screen shows. 2) Make sure that the Len and Width shows the applicable data: AIRPLANE MODEL DISPLAYED AIRPLANE DATA 737-700 <35M, <38M 737-800 <45M, <39.5M 737-900ER <45M, <39.5M (m) Do a check of the GPS Antenna Offset. 1) Set the AUTO/TEST/MANUAL switch to the MANUAL position until the GPS Antenna Offset screen shows. 2) Make sure that the Lat Axis shows Right 0 m. 3) Make that the Long Axis shows 10 m. ALL

I. Repeat ATC System Tests

SUBTASK 34-53-00-730-022 (1) Repeat the System Test for the other antenna. (2) Do the ATC System Tests again for the right or No. 2 system on the upper and lower antennas. NOTE: To meet FAR requirements both the left and right systems must be tested on both upper and lower antennas. (a) To test the right system, put the ATC select switch to the No. 2 position.

SUBTASK 34-53-00-080-004 (2) Disconnect and remove the antenna coupler, if installed. 34-53-00 SUBTASK 34-53-00-080-005 (3) Disconnect and remove the ATC test set. SUBTASK 34-53-00-860-051 (4) Do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. SUBTASK 34-53-00-860-052 (5) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN

34-53-00-730-807ATC System - System Test (With the AVX-10K Test Set)PDF p. 1000

7. ATC System - System Test (With the AVX-10K Test Set) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

WARNING USE AN ANTENNA COUPLER WITH THE RAMP TESTER TO SIMULATE AN AIR MODE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THE AIRPLANE WILL TRANSMIT ALTITUDE. YOU CAN ACCIDENTALLY CAUSE TCAS TARGETS. AIRCRAFT IN THE AREA WILL CHANGE DIRECTION QUICKLY TO GO AWAY FROM THESE TARGETS. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO AIRCRAFT . (1) This system test is a full check of the Air Traffic Control (ATC) system. The system test first does the ATC - Operational Test and then uses the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, to examine the left and right ATC systems. (2) The XPDR Mode of the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, provides flight line test capability for the Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System (ATCRBS), Mode S transponders. The auto test satisfies the 24 month ATC transponder maintenance check requirements. (3) The AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, can also test airplanes with Automatic Dependent Surveillance - Broadcast (ADS-B) function for DO 260, DO 260A, and DO 260B compliant transponders. The ADS-B tests are not included with the AUTO TEST . These tests satisfy the ADS-B Out 24 month ATC transponder maintenance check requirements. (4) Details of individual tests conducted during the AUTO TEST can be stored as files on the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186. Tests can be run individually by opening the associated ribbon prior to running the test. (5) Different classes of transponders are tested to built-in test limits by selection of configuration files. If the class of transponder is unknown, generic configuration files are provided for ATCRBS and Mode S transponders that apply the widest system limits. (6) Mode S Transponder level is automatically determined when running a test. (7) The test is applicable to the left and the right ATC system. Set the transponder select switch on the ATC control panel to the applicable position to do a test of that system. (8) This Predictive Maintenance & Enhanced Troubleshooting (PMET) procedure is optional and the results are for evaluation purposes only. No action is required as a result of this procedure if a flight deck effect or other observed fault does not exist. The recommendations are made to show best practices to make sure that maximum aircraft reliability is reached. If a flight deck effect or other observed fault exists, it must be corrected with accepted procedures. 34-53-00

E. Prepare for the System Test

SUBTASK 34-53-00-580-004 (1) If the ADS-B tests will be run as part of the ATC System test the airplane location must let the Global Positioning System (GPS) antennas have a clear view of the GPS satellites. SUBTASK 34-53-00-860-083 (2) Make sure that these systems are operational: (a) DFCS - DIGITAL FLIGHT CONTROL SYSTEM - ADJUSTMENT/TEST , PAGEBLOCK 22-11-00/501 (b) ADIRS - AIR DATA INERTIAL REFERENCE SYSTEM - ADJUSTMENT/TEST , PAGEBLOCK 34-21-00/501 (c) MMR - INSTRUMENT LANDING SYSTEM - ADJUSTMENT/TEST , PAGEBLOCK 34-31-00/501 34-53-00 (d) ATC - AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL (ATC) SYSTEM - ADJUSTMENT/TEST , 34-53-00/501 (e) FMCS - FLIGHT MANAGEMENT COMPUTER SYSTEM - ADJUSTMENT/TEST , PAGEBLOCK 34-61-00/501. SUBTASK 34-53-00-710-009 (3) Do this task: Air Traffic Control System - Operational Test, TASK 34-53-00-710-801. SUBTASK 34-53-00-860-084 (4) Set the Captain and First Officer (F/O) altimeter to 29.92 in/Hg (101.32 kPa). SUBTASK 34-53-00-860-085 (5) Set a desired heading on the Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) Mode Control Panel (MCP) HEADING window. SUBTASK 34-53-00-860-086 (6) Set a desired altitude in the DFCS MCP Selected Altitude window. NOTE: This test can be accomplished with any altitude. SUBTASK 34-53-00-860-087 (7) Select a Flight ID. (a) Select the RTE function key on the Flight Management Computer (FMC) Control Display Unit (CDU). (b) Make sure that page 1 is shown. 1) If it is necessary, push the next page function key on the CDU until page 1 is shown. (c) Enter a Flight ID on the CDU scratchpad (i.e. BOE1234). (d) Select LSK 2R on the CDU. SUBTASK 34-53-00-860-088 (8) On the ATC control panel do these steps: (a) Set the code switches to a desired ATC ID code. NOTE: Use the ATC ID code 7776 or the Mode A code specified by the local ATC authority. Do not use codes 7500, 7600-7677, 7700-7775 and 7777. These are emergency codes. (b) Set the ATC transponder select switch to the No. 1 position. (c) Set the mode select switch to the ALT ON position. (d) Set the ALT source switch to the No. 1 (or No. 2) air data source position. SUBTASK 34-53-00-760-002 (9) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name D 18 C00451 LANDING GEAR AURAL WARN SUBTASK 34-53-00-860-089 (10) Put the airplane in the air mode with the Built-In-Test Equipment (BITE) in the Proximity Switch Electronic Unit (PSEU) (TASK 32-09-00-860-801). 34-53-00 SUBTASK 34-53-00-840-015 (11) Prepare the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, for the ATC system test. NOTE: The AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, has an ‘‘auto test’’ function which includes a configuration for testing in accordance with FAR 43, Appendix F . Ramp test set operating instructions provides charts, distance limitations and required airplane antenna configurations for satisfactory ramp test set results. It is recommended that the ramp test set operator have the most current operating instructions for the ramp test set and be familiar with its operation when determining the acceptability of transponder results and compliance with FAR 43, Appendix F . NOTE: The software version for the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, should be version 3.1.10 or higher for the ATC system test. To view the current version, select system settings, and then select hardware software revision. (a) For the flat antenna connection, mount the Directional Antenna on the Test Sets quick disconnect inserts at the top of the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, and connect the Directional Antenna ANT Connector to the Test Set ANT Connector via the 12 in. (30 cm) coaxial cable. NOTE: You can use the direct cable connection procedure to perform this test. If you do the direct cable connection, follow the instructions in the ramp test set operations manual. WARNING USE AN ANTENNA COUPLER WITH THE RAMP TESTER TO SIMULATE AN AIR MODE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , THE AIRPLANE WILL TRANSMIT ALTITUDE. YOU CAN ACCIDENTALLY CAUSE TCAS TARGETS. AIRCRAFT IN THE AREA WILL CHANGE DIRECTION QUICKLY TO GO AWAY FROM THESE TARGETS. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO AIRCRAFT . (b) For the antenna coupler method connection, install the UC-584 universal transponder antenna coupler, COM-18775, over the antenna under test. NOTE: Refer to the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, Operation Manual for the antenna coupler mounting procedure. (c) Push the POWER Key to energize the Test Set On. Open the Transponder ribbon and click XPDR - Auto icon to start the test application. NOTE: Self Test on the AVX-10K is initiated manually. Refer to the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, Operation Manual for the full Self Test procedure. (d) Click on the SETUP tab to show the setup parameters. NOTE: Refer to the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, Operation Manual for detailed information on setup. NOTE: Setup XPDR Screen contains parameters which determine operational characteristics of the XPDR Functional Mode. Unless otherwise stated, last used values are retained on Power-up. 1) For the flat antenna connection, do these steps: a) Select RF PORT : Set to ANTENNA. b) Select DiversityTest: Set to On. Top and Bottom tabs will be displayed. Select TOP or BOTTOM tab depending on which aircraft antenna is under test. 34-53-00 c) Select Antenna Settings and Top or Bottom ANT RANGE: Set to setup range from AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, antenna to the Unit Under Test (UUT) Antenna. NOTE: The TOP tab is only available when Diversity Test is set to ON. d) Select Top or Bottom ANT HEIGHT : Set to setup height from AVX-10K antenna to the UUT Antenna. NOTE: The lower antenna is approximately 4 ft (1 m) above ground level. The upper antenna is approximately 18 ft (5 m) above ground level. e) Select ANT GAIN (dBi): set 1.03 GHz and 1.09 GHz antenna gain to figures marked on supplied Directional Antenna. f) Select Cable Settings and Top or Bottom Antenna Cable Length: Set to length of cables being used. g) Select Cable Settings and Top or Bottom Antenna Cable Loss: Set to cable loss found on cable. 2) For the antenna coupler connection, do these steps: a) Select RF PORT : Select DIRECT W/COUPLER. b) Select Cable Settings then Top or Bottom CABLE LOSS: Set to loss found on cable. c) Select Coupler Setting then Top or Bottom COUPLER LOSS: Set to loss found on coupler. 3) Select UUT ADDRESS: Set to AUTO (defaults to AUTO on power-up). AUTO selection Mode S address is obtained via ATCRBS/Mode S All Call (FAR Part 43, Appendix F approved method). NOTE: Refer to the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, Operation Manual for more detailed information on UUT Address selection. 4) Select DIVERSITY: Set to ON. NOTE: If Diversity Isolation Test is enabled, make sure that the Antenna Coupler with 50-ohm load is installed to the top or bottom UUT antenna prior to running the test. Refer to AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, Operation Manual for mounting procedure. NOTE: For the DIVERSITY test, the test set must be at a distance of less than 50 ft (15 m) from the airplane antenna. 5) Select Advanced Settings then Check All UUT Capability: Set to YES. (e) For the flat antenna connection, position the Test set ≤50 feet from and in line of sight with the UUT antenna. (f) For the flat antenna connection, put the UC-584 universal transponder antenna coupler, COM-18775, over the ATC antenna not under test. 1) If it is necessary, move the Test Set so that it is not in the line of sight of the top ATC antenna. NOTE: This step is optional if testing the bottom antenna and using the coupler on the top antenna is not possible or practical. (g) For the antenna coupler connection, put a second UC-584 universal transponder antenna coupler, COM-18775, over the ATC antenna not under test. 1) Add a 50-ohm load on the Radio Frequency (RF) connector of the coupler. 34-53-00 F . ATC System Test SUBTASK 34-53-00-730-041 (1) Do the ATC System Test: NOTE: When first powered-up, the Test Set displays blank data fields. The last test results are displayed while Test Set remains powered on. (a) Click the Top or Bottom tabs on the AVX-10K ramp test set, COM-23186, to return to XPDR Auto Test Screen. (b) Push the Test Configuration field to show the XPDR CONFIG parameters and select the desired configuration file. 34-53-01-000-801ATC Antenna RemovalPDF p. 1017

2. ATC Antenna Removal (Figure 401)

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 123 Forward Cargo Compartment - Left 124 Forward Cargo Compartment - Right 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

B. Removal Procedure

SUBTASK 34-53-01-860-001 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name B 5 C00186 ATC 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 14 C00188 ATC 2 E 14 C01194 ATC ANT SWITCH SUBTASK 34-53-01-020-001 (2) Remove the ATC antenna [3]: (a) Remove the bolts [4] that attach the ATC antenna [3] to the airplane structure. CAUTION MOVE THE ANTENNA ONLY AS FAR AS NECESSARY TO DISCONNECT THE CABLES. DAMAGE TO THE ANTENNA CABLES CAN OCCUR IF YOU PULL THE CABLES. (b) Move the ATC antenna [3] away from the airplane structure to get access to the coaxial connector [1]. (c) Disconnect the coaxial connector [1] from the ATC antenna [3]. NOTE: Do not let the coaxial connector retract into the fuselage. (d) Remove the ATC antenna [3] and O-ring [2]. 1) Discard the O-ring [2]. 34-53-01 (e) Put a protective cover over the electrical connector on the ATC antenna [3].

34-53-01-000-802ATC Antenna with Gasket - RemovalPDF p. 1020

3. ATC Antenna with Gasket - Removal (Figure 402)

A. General

(1) This procedure is used for the removal of antennas that use Aerobond or HI-TAK gaskets per 737-SL-20-045. (a) As a full certification test of the gasket was not done, it is recommended to do the steps that follow: (b) Do a visual inspection of the gasket and the mating surface, each D check. (c) Do a check for deterioration and corrosion on the antenna and gasket after their removal. (d) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion and fretting caused by the antenna gasket. 1) Remove any corrosion and fretting on the airplane skin.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 123 Forward Cargo Compartment - Left 124 Forward Cargo Compartment - Right 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

C. Removal Procedure

SUBTASK 34-53-01-860-007 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name B 5 C00186 ATC 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 14 C00188 ATC 2 E 14 C01194 ATC ANT SWITCH SUBTASK 34-53-01-020-002 (2) Remove the ATC antenna [3]: (a) Remove the bolts [4] that attach the ATC antenna [3] to the airplane structure. CAUTION MOVE THE ANTENNA ONLY AS FAR AS NECESSARY TO DISCONNECT THE CABLES. DAMAGE TO THE ANTENNA CABLES CAN OCCUR IF YOU PULL THE CABLES. (b) Move the ATC antenna [3] away from the airplane structure to get access to the coaxial cable [1]. (c) Disconnect the coaxial cable [1] from the ATC antenna [3]. NOTE: Do not let the coaxial cable [1] retract into the fuselage. (d) Remove the ATC antenna [3]. 34-53-01 (e) Remove and discard the ATC gasket [5] NOTE: For the Aerobond gasket, special attention must be used to remove the gel material residue to prevent silicone oil contamination on other parts of the airplane skin, which may cause paint adhesion difficulties. (f) Put a protective cover over the electrical connector on the ATC antenna [3].

ATC Antenna Installation SUBTASK 34-53-01-860-002 (1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name B 5 C00186 ATC 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 14 C00188 ATC 2 E 14 C01194 ATC ANT SWITCH SUBTASK 34-53-01-110-001 WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THESE MATERIALS. PUT ON A PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THESE MATERIALS. KEEP THESE MATERIALS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THESE MATERIALS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (2) Clean the airplane mating surface with Series 84 solvent, B01004 (TASK 20-30-84-910-801). (a) Make cotton wiper, G00034, moist (not soaked) with solvent. (b) Rub the airplane mating surface with cotton wiper, G00034, until the surface is clean. SUBTASK 34-53-01-300-001 (3) If the airplane mating surface has corrosion or unwanted material, do these steps to prepare the airplane mating surface: (a) Remove the corrosion or unwanted material from the airplane mating surface, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Aluminum and Aluminum Alloys, TASK 51-21-31-350-801. (b) Apply a layer of chemical conversion coating to the airplane mating surface, do this task: Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero, Bonderite M-CR ALCRM 1200 Aero, or Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero Application Process, TASK 51-21-41-370-802. SUBTASK 34-53-01-420-001 (4) Install the Air Traffic Control (ATC) antenna [3]. (a) Remove the protective cover from the antenna coaxial connector [1]. (b) Install the new O-ring [2] on the ATC antenna [3]. (c) Apply sealant, A00247, to the threads of the bolts [4]. (d) Examine the coaxial connector [1] for bent or broken pins, dirt, and damage. (e) Connect the coaxial connector [1] to the ATC antenna [3]. 34-53-01 (f) Put the ATC antenna [3] in the correct position on the airplane surface. (g) Install three of the four bolts [4]. 1) Tighten the bolts [4] to 35 in-lb (3.95 N·m). SUBTASK 34-53-01-760-001 (5) Measure the resistance between the ATC antenna baseplate and the airplane skin with an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. (a) Use the empty bolt hole to get access to the antenna baseplate. (b) Make sure that the resistance is less than 0.001 ohm (1 milliohm). SUBTASK 34-53-01-420-002 (6) Install the last bolt [4]. (a) Tighten the bolt [4] to 35 in-lb (3.95 N·m). SUBTASK 34-53-01-390-002 (7) Apply aerodynamic sealant. NOTE: Operators can defer the application of the aero-sealant in the antenna installation until next “A” check or overnight maintenance stop to prevent a flight delay. The deferral of the application of sealant must not exceed a maximum of eight weeks (SL 20-043). (a) Apply an aerodynamic fillet seal around the base of the antenna [3] with sealant, A00247 (TASK 51-31-00-390-806, TASK 20-30-11-910-801). (b) Let the sealant dry for the correct cure time. SUBTASK 34-53-01-860-003 (8) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name B 5 C00186 ATC 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 14 C00188 ATC 2 E 14 C01194 ATC ANT SWITCH

SUBTASK 34-53-01-300-002 (3) If the airplane mating surface has corrosion or unwanted material, do these steps to prepare the airplane mating surface: (a) Remove the corrosion or unwanted material from the airplane mating surface. To remove the corrosion or unwanted material, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Aluminum and Aluminum Alloys, TASK 51-21-31-350-801. (b) Apply a layer of chemical conversion coating to the airplane mating surface. To apply the coating, do this task: Bonderite M-CR 600 Aero, Bonderite M-CR ALCRM 1200 Aero, or Bonderite M-CR 1200S Aero Application Process, TASK 51-21-41-370-802. SUBTASK 34-53-01-420-004 (4) Install the Air Traffic Control (ATC) antenna. (a) Remove the protective cover from the antenna electrical connector. (b) Remove and discard the O-ring (if installed) from ATC antenna [3]. (c) Remove the protective film from each side of the gasket [5]. NOTE: Reference the Aircraft Illustrated Parts Catalog for the gasket part number. (d) Put the gasket [5] on the ATC antenna [3]. (e) Examine the coaxial connector [1] for bent or broken pins, dirt, and damage. (f) Connect the coaxial connector [1] to the ATC antenna [3]. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY SEALANT TO THE EDGES OF THE ANTENNA. THE GASKET RELEASES THE MOISTURE. IF YOU SEAL THE EDGES, THE MOISTURE WILL STAY . THIS CAN CAUSE CORROSION DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE, AND ANTENNA MATING SURFACES. (g) Put the ATC antenna [3] in the correct position on the airplane surface. (h) Install three of the four bolts [4]. 1) Tighten the bolts [4] to 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m). NOTE: Since the gel material of the gasket is compressible, the bolts need to be re-torqued 15 minutes of the installation. SUBTASK 34-53-01-760-002 (5) Measure the resistance between the ATC antenna baseplate and the airplane skin with an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. NOTE: Use the empty bolt hole to get access to the antenna baseplate. (a) Make sure that the resistance is less than 0.001 ohm. SUBTASK 34-53-01-420-005 (6) Install the last bolt [4]. (a) Tighten the bolt [4] to 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m). NOTE: Since the gel material of the gasket is compressible, the bolt must be re-torqued 15 minutes of the installation. 34-53-01 SUBTASK 34-53-01-860-009 (7) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name B 5 C00186 ATC 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 14 C00188 ATC 2 E 14 C01194 ATC ANT SWITCH

SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-074 (2) Set the SOURCE switch on the instrument switching module to the AUTO position. SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-003 (3) Set the display select switch on the captain's and first officer's EFIS control panels to the VOR position.

E. DME Self Test

SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-075 (1) Make sure that the DME 1 and DME 2 are not tuned to a local station's frequency. SUBTASK 34-55-00-740-002 (2) Push and hold the TEST button on the captain's navigation control panel to start the DME 1 self test. (a) Make sure that the DME 2 shows dashes on the displays during the DME 1 self test. (b) Make sure that the DME 1 has a flag on the displays for approximately two seconds. (c) Make sure that the DME 1 shows dashes on the displays until the end of the test. SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-005 (3) Release the TEST button on the captain's navigation control panel. 34-55-00 SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-046 (4) To get access to the proximity switch electronics unit, open this access panel: Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-006 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE CONTROL SURFACES AND LANDING GEAR DOOR AREAS. THE CONTROL SURFACES, THE LANDING GEAR, AND THE LANDING GEAR DOORS CAN MOVE WHEN YOU DO THE AIR MODE SIMULATION. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (5) Put SYS No. 1 in the Air Mode. Do this task:Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. SUBTASK 34-55-00-730-002 (6) Push and hold the TEST button on the captain's navigation control panel to start the DME 1 self test. (a) Make sure that the self test sequence for DME 1 did not start. SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-007 (7) Release the TEST button on the captain's navigation control panel. SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-008 (8) Put SYS No. 1 in the Ground Mode. Do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. SUBTASK 34-55-00-730-003 (9) Set the VHF NAV switch on the instrument switching module to the BOTH ON 2 position. SUBTASK 34-55-00-730-004 (10) Push and hold the TEST button on the first officer's navigation control panel to start the DME 2 self test. (a) Make sure that the DME 1 shows dashes on the displays during the DME 2 self test. (b) Make sure that the DME 2 has a flag on the displays for approximately two seconds. (c) Make sure that the DME 2 shows dashes on the displays until the end of the test. SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-009 (11) Release the TEST button on the first officer's navigation control panel. SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-010 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE CONTROL SURFACES AND LANDING GEAR DOOR AREAS. THE CONTROL SURFACES, THE LANDING GEAR, AND THE LANDING GEAR DOORS CAN MOVE WHEN YOU DO THE AIR MODE SIMULATION. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (12) Put SYS No. 2 in the Air Mode. Do this task:Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. SUBTASK 34-55-00-730-005 (13) Push and hold the TEST button on the first officer's navigation control panel to start the DME 2 self test. (a) Make sure that the self test sequence for DME 2 did not start. 34-55-00 SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-011 (14) Release the TEST button on the first officer's navigation control panel. SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-012 (15) Put SYS No. 2 in the Ground Mode. Do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. SUBTASK 34-55-00-860-047 (16) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door SUBTASK 34-55-00-730-032 (17) Set the SOURCE switch on the instrument switching module to the AUTO position.

2. DME Antenna Removal (Figure 401)

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 123 Forward Cargo Compartment - Left 124 Forward Cargo Compartment - Right 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

B. DME Antenna Removal

SUBTASK 34-55-11-860-001 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name B 3 C00190 RADIO NAVIGATION DME 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 14 C00192 RADIO NAVIGATION DME 2 SUBTASK 34-55-11-020-001 (2) Remove the DME antenna [3]: (a) Remove the bolts [4] from the DME antenna base. CAUTION LOWER THE ANTENNA ONLY AS FAR AS REQUIRED TO DISCONNECT THE COAXIAL CONNECTOR. DAMAGE TO THE CABLE CAN OCCUR IF YOU PULL THE CABLE. (b) Lower the DME antenna [3], until access to the coaxial connector [1] can be gotten. (c) Disconnect the coaxial connector [1] from the DME antenna [3]. (d) Remove the DME antenna [3]. (e) Remove and discard the O-ring [2] from the DME antenna [3]. (f) Put a protective cover on the coaxial connector [1].

34-55-11-000-802DME Antenna with Gasket RemovalPDF p. 1069

3. DME Antenna with Gasket Removal (Figure 402)

A. General

(1) This task is used for the removal of DME antennas that use Aerobond or HI-TAK gaskets per 737-SL-20-045. (2) As a full certification test of the gasket was not done, it is recommended to do thee steps: (a) Do a visual inspection of the gasket and the mating surface, each D check. (b) Do a check for deterioration and corrosion on the DME antenna and gasket after their removal. (c) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion and fretting caused by the DME antenna gasket. 1) Remove any corrosion and fretting on the airplane skin.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 123 Forward Cargo Compartment - Left 124 Forward Cargo Compartment - Right 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

C. DME Antenna with Gasket Removal

SUBTASK 34-55-11-860-007 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name B 3 C00190 RADIO NAVIGATION DME 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 14 C00192 RADIO NAVIGATION DME 2 SUBTASK 34-55-11-020-002 (2) Remove the DME antenna [3]: (a) Remove the bolts [4] from the DME antenna [3] base. CAUTION MOVE THE ANTENNA ONLY AS FAR AS NECESSARY TO DISCONNECT THE CABLES. DAMAGE TO THE ANTENNA CABLES CAN OCCUR IF YOU PULL THE CABLES. (b) Lower the DME antenna [3] until access to the coaxial connector [1] can be gotten. (c) Disconnect the coaxial connector [1] from the DME antenna [3]. NOTE: Do not let the coaxial cable retract into the fuselage. (d) Remove the DME antenna [3]. 34-55-11 (e) Remove and discard the DME gasket [5]. NOTE: For the Aerobond gasket, special attention must be used to remove the gel material residue to prevent silicone oil contamination on other parts of the airplane skin, that may cause paint adhesion difficulties. (f) Put a protective cover on the coaxial connector [1].

34-55-11-400-802DME Antenna with Gasket InstallationPDF p. 1077

5. DME Antenna with Gasket Installation (Figure 402)

A. General

(1) This task is used for the installation of DME antennas with Aerobond or HI-TAK gaskets per 737-SL-20-045. (2) As a full certification test of the gasket was not done, it is recommended to do these steps: (a) Do a visual inspection of the gasket and the mating surface, each D check. (b) Do a check for deterioration and corrosion on the DME antenna and gasket after their removal. (c) Do a check of the airplane skin for corrosion and fretting caused by the DME antenna gasket. 1) Remove any corrosion and fretting on the airplane skin.

34-57-00-730-802Automatic Direction Finder System - System TestPDF p. 1093

2. Automatic Direction Finder System - System Test

A. General

(1) Some of the tests need radio reception from local Amplitude Modulation (AM) commercial broadcast stations or Automatic Direction Finder (ADF) beacon transmitting stations. NOTE: ADF bearing checks on the ground, in hangars, or near other airplanes, metal buildings and equipment, etc. may show inaccurate bearings or weak signals.

C. Location Zones

SUBTASK 34-57-01-020-001 (3) Remove the ADF antenna [1]: (a) Loosen the mounting bolts [4] and until they disengage from the airplane nutplates. CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU USE THE SEALANT REMOVAL TOOL TO BREAK THE SEAL. TOO MUCH FORCE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE SKIN, THE ANTENNA CABLE OR THE ADF ANTENNA. (b) Use force around the ADF antenna [1] with the sealant removal tool, COM-2481, until the seal is fully broken. CAUTION LIFT THE ADF ANTENNA ONLY AS FAR AS NECESSARY TO DISCONNECT THE CABLE. DAMAGE TO THE ANTENNA CABLE CAN OCCUR IF YOU PULL THE CABLE. (c) Lift the ADF antenna [1] until you can get access to the electrical connecctor [3]. (f) Put a protective cover on the electrical connecctor [3].

Prepare for the Installation SUBTASK 34-57-01-860-023 (1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 4 C01382 RADIO NAVIGATION ADF 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name 020 POST SB 737-34-2208; 043, 044 POST SB 737-34-2302 A 17 C01383 RADIO NAVIGATION ADF 2 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH ADF ANTENNA This circuit breaker is inoperative and should remain open: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name 006, 007, 013, 014, 018, 019, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 020 PRE SB 737-34-2208 A 17 C01383 RADIO NAVIGATION ADF 2 (INOP) ALL; AIRPLANES WITH ADF ANTENNA SUBTASK 34-57-01-110-001 (2) Clean the airplane skin (TASK 51-21-00-100-801). (a) Remove the old sealant from the airplane skin in the Automatic Direction Finder (ADF) antenna [1] area. 34-57-01 (b) Clean the mating surface with solvent, B00083. SUBTASK 34-57-01-620-001 (3) If the airplane skin has corrosion or other damage, do these steps: (a) To remove the corrosion, do this task: Removal and Control of Corrosion for Aluminum and Aluminum Alloys, TASK 51-21-31-350-801. (b) Apply a layer of coating, C00064, on the airplane skin in the area where the ADF antenna [1] touches the skin.

G. ADF Antenna Installation

SUBTASK 34-57-01-420-001 (1) Install the ADF antenna [1]. (a) Apply a thin layer of compound, A00230, to the antenna base. (b) Apply the Frekote 700-NC non-peelable parting agent, G02497 (preferred), or Frekote 710-NC non-peelable parting agent, G50313 (preferred), or Frekote 44-NC non-peelable parting agent, G50335 (alternative), or Frekote 48 NC non-peelable parting agent, G50711 (alternative), to the ADF antenna base. (c) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, on the new O-ring [2] and O-ring groove. (d) Install the new O-ring [2] on the ADF antenna [1]. (e) Remove the protective cover from the electrical connecctor [3]. (f) Connect the electrical connecctor [3] to the ADF antenna [1]. (g) Put the ADF antenna [1] into position on the airplane surface. (h) Lightly tighten the bolts [4] in a diagonal pattern to hold the ADF antenna [1] in the correct position. NOTE: Refer to the IPC for the bolt part number. CAUTION TIGHTEN THE BOLTS MANUALLY TO THE CORRECT TORQUE VALUE. OPERATION OF POWER OR AIR TOOLS TO TIGHTEN THE BOLTS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ADF ANTENNA SURFACE. (i) Manually tighten the bolts [4] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). (j) Remove the unwanted compound, A00230, from around the edge of the ADF antenna [1].

H. Resistance Measurement (Preferred)

SUBTASK 34-57-01-760-001 (1) Do a check of the electrical continuity between the ADF antenna [1] baseplate and the airplane skin. (a) Loosen one bolt [4] from the ADF antenna [1]. (b) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bolt counterbore and the airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.001 ohm (1 milliohm) or less. (c) If the resistance measurement caused damage, apply the sealant, A02315, or sealant, A00247, to the damaged area of the airplane skin. (d) Manually tighten the bolt [4] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). 34-57-01

I. Resistance Measurement (Alternate)

SUBTASK 34-57-01-760-002 (1) Do a check of the electrical continuity from the inside of the airplane between the ADF antenna [1] baseplate and the airplane skin. (a) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the ADF antenna [1] baseplate and the airplane skin (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.001 ohm (1 milliohm) or less. (b) If the resistance measurement caused damage, apply the sealant, A02315, or sealant, A00247, to the damaged area of the airplane skin.

J. Aerodynamic Fillet Seal Installation

SUBTASK 34-57-01-390-001 (1) Fill the bolts [4] counterbores with approximately 0.3 in. (7.6 mm) of cotton plug. SUBTASK 34-57-01-390-002 (2) Seal all the bolts [4] with sealant, A02315, or sealant, A00247, until flush with the ADF antenna [1] surface (TASK 51-31-00-390-805). SUBTASK 34-57-01-390-003 (3) Apply a fillet seal with sealant, A02315, or sealant, A00247, around the base of the ADF antenna [1] (TASK 51-31-00-390-804). NOTE: Operators can defer the application of the aero-sealant in the antenna installation until next “A” check or overnight maintenance stop to prevent a flight delay. The deferral of the application of sealant must not exceed a maximum of eight weeks (SL 20-043). SUBTASK 34-57-01-390-004 (4) Use the hardwood or plastic fillet smoothing spatula, STD-810, to make a smooth 45-degree bead. SUBTASK 34-57-01-140-002 (5) Remove unwanted sealant from the area around the ADF antenna [1] base. SUBTASK 34-57-01-390-005 (6) Let the sealant dry for the correct cure time.

K. ADF Antenna Installation Test

NOTE: This tryout is to make sure the GPS is in a zero energy state. SUBTASK 34-58-00-860-010 (1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 A 3 C01378 RADIO NAVIGATION NAV CONT PNL 1 B 1 C01376 RADIO NAVIGATION NAV SNSR DC-1 34-58-00 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 10 C01377 RADIO NAVIGATION NAV SNSR DC-2 A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2 A 15 C01379 RADIO NAVIGATION NAV CONT PNL 2 SUBTASK 34-58-00-710-005 (2) Do these steps at the CDU: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU. (b) Push the line select key (LSK) that is adjacent to <INDEX. (c) Push the LSK that is adjacent to <POS. (d) Push the NEXT PAGE key on the CDU. (e) Make sure the GPS position does not show on the screen. NOTE: Wait at least 5 minutes to make sure the position does not show on the CDU.

2. Global Positioning System - Operational Test

A. General

(1) This task does a GPS position check.

B. References

Reference Title 09-11-00-580-801 Maintenance Towing (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-58-00-860-008 (1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2 SUBTASK 34-58-00-580-001 (2) Move the airplane to a position where the GPS antennas have a clear view of the GPS satellites. To move the airplane, do this task: Maintenance Towing, TASK 09-11-00-580-801. SUBTASK 34-58-00-710-001 (3) Do these steps to see the GPS position on the CDU: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU. (b) Push the line select key (LSK) that is adjacent to <INDEX. (c) Push the LSK that is adjacent to <POS. (d) Push the NEXT PAGE key on the CDU. (e) Make sure the steps that follow occur: 1) The GPS L position on the CDU agrees with the known airplane position. NOTE: As much as 5 minutes of time can be necessary for the positions to show on the CDU. 34-58-00 2) The GPS R position on the CDU agrees with the known airplane position. NOTE: As much as 5 minutes of time can be necessary for the positions to show on the CDU.

34-58-00-730-802Global Positioning System - System TestPDF p. 1136

3. Global Positioning System - System Test

A. General

(1) This procedure does a GPS interface check. (2) The airplane must be moved to a position where the GPS antennas have a clear view of the GPS satellites.

B. References

Reference Title 09-11-00-580-801 Maintenance Towing (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Global Positioning System System Test

SUBTASK 34-58-00-580-002 (1) Move the airplane to a position where the GPS antennas have a clear view of the GPS satellites, do this task: Maintenance Towing, TASK 09-11-00-580-801. SUBTASK 34-58-00-860-004 (2) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2 SUBTASK 34-58-00-710-004 (3) Do these steps to see the GPS position on the CDU: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU. (b) Make sure that the steps that follow occur: 1) The time on the CDU agrees with the known time. 2) The date on the CDU agrees with the known date. (c) Push the line select key (LSK) that is adjacent to <INDEX. (d) Push the LSK that is adjacent to <POS. (e) Push the NEXT PAGE key on the CDU. (f) Make sure that the steps that follow occur: 34-58-00 1) The GPS L position on the CDU agrees with the known airplane position. NOTE: As much as 5 minutes of time can be necessary for the positions to show on the CDU. 2) The GPS R position on the CDU agrees with the known airplane position. NOTE: As much as 5 minutes of time can be necessary for the positions to show on the CDU. SUBTASK 34-58-00-710-003 (4) Do these steps to do a check of the GPS annunciator on the IRS MSU (P5 panel): (a) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 1) Make sure that the GPS L position goes out of view on the CDU. 2) Make sure that the GPS R position stays in view on the CDU. 3) Make sure that the GPS annunciator on the IRS MSU (P5) stays off. (b) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2 1) Make sure that the GPS R position goes out of view on the CDU. 2) Make sure that the GPS L position stays out of view on the CDU. 3) Make sure that the GPS annunciator on the IRS MSU (P5) comes on after approximately 10 seconds. (c) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-1 Row Col Number Name A 2 C01479 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 1 F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name A 13 C01480 RADIO NAVIGATION MMR 2 (d) Make sure that the GPS annunciator on the IRS MSU goes off. (e) Stop for approximately 5 minutes until the GPS L and GPS R positions are shown again. SUBTASK 34-58-00-710-006 (5) Do a check of GPS time and date: (a) Push the INIT REF key on the CDU. (b) Make sure that the steps that follow occur: 1) The time on the CDU agrees with the known time. 2) The date on the CDU agrees with the known date.

D. Removal Procedure

CAUTION BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU USE THE SEALANT REMOVAL TOOL TO BREAK THE SEAL. TOO MUCH FORCE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE SKIN, AND OTHER COMPONENTS. (c) Use the sealant removal tool, COM-2481, to break the seal all around the GPS antenna [1]. CAUTION MOVE THE ANTENNA THE MINIMUM DISTANCE NECESSARY TO LET YOU TO DISCONNECT THE COAXIAL CONNECTOR. DAMAGE TO THE COAXIAL CABLE CAN OCCUR IF YOU PULL THE CABLE WITH TOO MUCH FORCE. (d) Carefully pull the GPS antenna [1] until you can get access to the coaxial connector [3]. (e) Disconnect the coaxial connector [3]. NOTE: Make sure that the coaxial cable and connector do not fall into the airplane fuselage. (f) Remove the GPS antenna [1] and the O-ring [4]. (g) Put protective covers on the coaxial connector [3].

G. GPS Antenna Installation

SUBTASK 34-58-02-390-006 (1) Prepare the GPS antenna [1] as follows: (a) Apply a layer of grease, D00633, on the new O-ring [4] and the O-ring groove. (b) Install the O-ring [4] on the GPS antenna [1]. 1) Make sure that the O-ring [4] is not damaged and is installed correctly in the o-ring groove. (c) Apply a layer of sealant, A00247, on the shank of the screws [2]. SUBTASK 34-58-02-420-004 (2) Install the GPS antenna [1]. (a) Remove the protective covers from the coaxial connector [3]. (b) Examine the coaxial connector [3] for dirt and damage. (c) Connect the coaxial connector [3]. (d) Tighten the coaxial connector [3] to 8 in-lb (0.9 N·m) - 12 in-lb (1.4 N·m). 34-58-02 (e) Apply a large quantity of silicone compound, D00254, to the outside coaxial connector and at the exterior connector/antenna interface. (f) Put the GPS antenna [1] into its position on the airplane. (g) Install the three screws [2] that hold the GPS antenna [1]. WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THESE MATERIALS. PUT ON A PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THESE MATERIALS. KEEP THESE MATERIALS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THESE MATERIALS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (h) Remove the unwanted sealant, A00247, from around the antenna with Series 84 solvent, B01004 (TASK 20-30-84-910-801). SUBTASK 34-58-02-760-002 (3) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the GPS antenna [1] and airplane skin. (a) Use an non-intrinsically safe bonding meter, COM-614, between the base of the antenna and airplane skin. NOTE: You can get access to the base of the antenna through the hole for the last screw. 1) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.001 ohm (1 milliohm) or less. SUBTASK 34-58-02-420-005 (4) Install the last screw [2] that holds the GPS antenna [1]. SUBTASK 34-58-02-420-006 WARNING DO NOT GET SOLVENTS IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THESE MATERIALS. PUT ON A PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE THESE MATERIALS. KEEP THESE MATERIALS AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . THESE MATERIALS ARE POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT . (5) Remove the unwanted sealant, A00247, from around the head of each screw [2] with Series 84 solvent, B01004 (TASK 20-30-84-910-801).

H. Aerodynamic Fillet Seal Installation

SUBTASK 34-58-02-390-007 (1) Apply a fillet seal with sealant, A02315, or sealant, A00247, around the base of the GPS antenna [1] (TASK 51-31-00-390-804). NOTE: Operators can defer the application of the aero-sealant in the antenna installation until next “A” check or overnight maintenance stop to prevent a flight delay. The deferral of the application of sealant must not exceed a maximum of eight weeks (SL 20-043). (a) Apply the sealant all around the edge of the GPS antenna [1]. 1) Make sure that no air bubbles are in the sealant. (b) Use a sufficient quantity of the sealant to permit you to make the surface smooth. 34-58-02 SUBTASK 34-58-02-390-008 (2) Make the bead into an aerodynamic fillet seal approximately 0.7 in. (17.8 mm) wide with the hardwood or plastic fillet smoothing spatula, STD-810 (TASK 51-31-00-390-804). SUBTASK 34-58-02-140-002 (3) Remove all the unwanted sealant from the area around the antenna. 34-61-00-470-805FMC Software Installation with a Portable Data LoaderPDF p. 1150

4. FMC Software Installation with a Portable Data Loader

A. General

(1) This procedure tells you how to install software into the Flight Management Computer (FMC) with a portable data loader. (a) The FMC usually contains these pieces of software: 1) Operational Program Software (OPS) 2) Navigation Database (NDB) 3) Software Options Database (OPC) 4) Model/Engine Database (MEDB). (b) The FMC can contain these pieces of optional software: 1) Performance Defaults Database (Perf Defaults) 2) ACARS Datalink Configuration Database (Adaptable Datalink Database (ADDB)) 3) Flight Plan Database 34-61-00 4) Loadable Default Data Base (LDDB). NOTE: When you install a complete set of the FMC software, you should install the OPS first. Loading the OPS will clear any loaded OPC, NDB, LDDB, and ADDB, therefore, these programs need to be reloaded. (2) If you install a full set of the FMC software, you must install the OPS first. The OPS installation erases all other software installed in the FMC. Also, performance factors that are changed by manual entry from the Control Display Unit (CDU) go back to their default values. (a) You must install the NDB and MEDB databases again after the installation of the OPS. If you do not install the customized OPC, the OPS will use default values. (b) You must install the optional databases, Perf Defaults or Datalink, again if your airline uses them. If you do not install a customized Perf Defaults or Datalink database the OPS will use default values. (3) If the PDL is connected to the DATA TRANSFER UNIT RECEPTACLE, you cannot use the ADL to load data. (4) A Portable Data Loader (PDL) is not a supplied part. Refer to the PDL supplier for instructions for operation. PDLs have a disk drive for software installation from disks. Some PDLs have an internal mass storage device. If the software is stored in the PDL, then disks are not necessary. (5) The MEDB installation erases the initially installed LDDB. Also the manually selected performance factors go back to their default values. (a) You must install the customized LDDB, given directly from the FMC supplier, again if your airline uses them. (6) The installation of the OPC, ADDB, LDDB or NDB does not erase other initially installed software. (7) Modern software loaders that meet the security requirements defined in ARINC 645-1 or newer are recommended to use. The procedures for modern software loaders will be marked as preferred for now and will be the only procedures available after removing floppy disk loaders procedures in the future. Please check with your Software Loader Supplier for current capabilities since this is still maturing across current and future software loaders.

34-61-00-470-806FMC Software CrossloadPDF p. 1158

5. FMC Software Crossload

A. General

(1) This procedure tells you how to crossload software from one FMC to the other FMC. A crossload will install the software into the second FMC significantly faster than the data loader. (a) The Flight Management Computer (FMC) usually contains these pieces of software: 1) Operational Program Software (OPS) 2) Navigation Database (NDB) 3) Software Options Database (OPC) 4) Model/Engine Database (MEDB). (b) The FMC can contain these pieces of optional software: 1) Performance Defaults Database (Perf Defaults) 2) ACARS Datalink Configuration Database (Adaptable Datalink Database (ADDB)) 3) Flight Plan Database 4) Loadable Default Data Base (LDDB). (2) If an OP PROGRAM or DATABASE crossload is carried out, all previously entered performance factors, such as F-F Factor, must be manually entered into the FMC. (3) If you install a full set of the FMC Software, you must install the OPS first. The OPS installation erases all other software installed in the FMC. Also, performance factors that are changed by manual entry from the Control Display Unit (CDU) go back to their default values. (a) You must install the NDB and MEDB databases again after the installation of the OPS. If you do not install the customized OPC, the OPS will use default values. (b) You must install the optional databases, Perf Defaults, Datalink, flight plan or LDDB, again if your airline uses them. If you do not install a customized Perf Defaults or Datalink database the OPS will use default values. (4) The MEDB installation erases the initially installed LDDB. Also, the manually selected performance factors go back to their default values. (a) You must install the customized LDDB, given directly from the FMC supplier, again if your airline uses them. (5) The installation of the OPC, ADDB, LDDB or NDB does not erase other initially installed software. (6) After a dual FMC power-up, the OP PROGRAM CROSSLOAD page or the DATABASE CROSSLOAD page is shown automatically on the CDU if the two FMCs have different software installed. (7) When the CROSSLOAD> prompt is shown on the FMCS BITE page, you can push the LSK to manually select the OP PROGRAM CROSSLOAD page or the DATABASE CROSSLOAD page.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 210 Subzone - Control Compartment - Body Station 178.00 to Body Station 259.50 34-61-00 056-063, 067-078, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 081 POST SB 737-34-2000 (Continued)

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-61-00-470-013 (1) Do these steps to crossload the software: (a) Make sure the CDU shows one of these two pages, the OP PROGRAM CROSSLOAD page or the DATABASE CROSSLOAD page. NOTE: The CROSSLOAD> prompt is not shown if an FMC is failed, or only one FMC is powered, or only one FMC is installed in a dual FMC configuration. NOTE: The OP PROGRAM CROSSLOAD page lets you install the operational program and databases into the other FMC. The DATABASE CROSSLOAD page lets you install only the databases into the other FMC. NOTE: If the OP PROGRAM INVALID page shows, you must set the FMC source select switch to the position shown on the CDU. (b) Push the CDU LSK next to COPY FROM LEFT(RIGHT) to select the FMC you want to copy from. NOTE: If you see the message SET FMC SOURCE SELECT TO BOTH-ON-L(R), make sure the switch is in the correct position. (c) Push the EXEC key on the CDU. (d) The CROSSLOAD IN PROGRESS message shows during the FMC crossload. (e) The CROSSLOAD COMPLETE message shows for a successful crossload. NOTE: The CROSSLOAD FAIL message is shown if the FMC crossload fails. Possible causes for a failure are loss of communication between the FMC's, loss of power to one FMC, or failure of the FMC receiving the data. A second attempt may be made to do the crossload. Select the INDEX prompt to return to the FMC BITE page. Then select the CROSSLOAD> prompt to repeat the crossload operation. NOTE: A database crossload failure causes the NEXT MISMATCH prompt to show with the CROSSLOAD COMPLETE message. The prompt can also show for mismatches in the analog input discretes or the performance factors. Select the NEXT MISMATCH prompt to continue. 6. FMC Software Configuration Check

A. General

(1) This procedure tells you how to check the Flight Management Computer (FMC) software installation. (2) You must know the correct part number for the FMC software. For the FMC to be an approved installation, software with the correct part number must be installed. 34-61-00

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 210 Subzone - Control Compartment - Body Station 178.00 to Body Station 259.50

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-004 (1) Do these steps to do a software configuration check of the FMC: 056-063, 067-078, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 081 POST SB 737-34-2000; AIRPLANES WITH DUAL FMC (a) Set the Flight Management Computer System (FMCS) transfer switch to the applicable position: 1) To check the software for the left FMC, set the FMCS transfer switch to the NORMAL position. 2) To check the software for the right FMC, set the FMCS transfer switch to the BOTH ON R position. ALL (b) Make sure that the Control Display Unit (CDU) display shows the IDENT 1/2 page. (c) Do these steps if the IDENT 1/2 page is not shown: 1) Push the INIT/REF key on both CDUs. 2) Push the LSK next to IDENTon both CDUs. (d) Do a check of the FMC operational program and navigational database software: 1) Make sure that the correct part number for the operational program shows below OP PROGRAM on the CDU. 2) Make sure that the correct part number for the navigation database shows below NAV DATA on the CDU. 3) Make sure that the correct date range shows below ACTIVE on the CDU. (e) Push the NEXT PAGE button on the CDU. (f) Make sure that the CDU display shows the IDENT 2/2 page. (g) Do a check of this FMC software: 1) Make sure that the correct part number for the software options database shows below SW OPTIONS on the CDU. NOTE: You must install the software options database for the FMC to operate. If you did not install a software options database the CDU will show DEFAULT050 below SW OPTIONS. 2) Make sure that the correct part number for the model/engine database shows below MODEL/ENGINE DATA on the CDU. NOTE: You must install the model/engine database for the FMC to operate. If INVALID shows on the CDU, the model/engine database was not installed. If PROGRAM PIN NOT IN MODEL/ENGINE DATABSE shows, the model/engine database installed does not match the airframe/engine program pin configuration. 3) Make sure that the correct part number is shown for any installed optional databases (Perf Defaults, Datalink, Flight plan or Loadable Default). 34-61-00 SUBTASK 34-61-00-470-025 (2) If a part number is not correct, do this task: FMC Software Installation with a Portable Data Loader, TASK 34-61-00-470-805

7. CDU Software Installation with a Portable Data Loader (AIRPLANES WITH LIQUID CRYSTAL DISPLAY CDU)

A. General

(1) This procedure tells you how to install software into the CDU with a portable data loader. (2) A Portable Data Loader (PDL) is not a supplied part. Refer to the PDL supplier for instructions for operation. PDLs have a disk drive for software installation from disks. Some PDLs have an internal mass storage device. If the software is stored in the PDL, then disks are not necessary. (3) Modern software loaders that meet the security requirements defined in ARINC 645-1 or newer are recommended to use. The procedures for modern software loaders will be marked as preferred for now and will be the only procedures available after removing floppy disk loaders procedures in the future. Please check with your Software Loader Supplier for current capabilities since this is still maturing across current and future software loaders.

9. FMC Diagnostic Data Transfer

A. General

(1) An Airborne Data Loader (ADL) or Portable Data Loader (PDL) is necessary for this procedure. (2) This procedure tells you how to transfer diagnostic data from the Left and Right FMC to a 3.5 inch diskette. 056-063, 067-078, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 081 POST SB 737-34-2000 NOTE: A single diskette has sufficient capacity to hold data from both FMCs. ALL

Zone Area 210 Subzone - Control Compartment - Body Station 178.00 to Body Station 259.50

C. FMC Diagnostic Data Transfer

SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-008 (1) Use the FMCPREP PC software to format the disk or prepare the USB flash drive. (a) You must make a copy of the FMCPREP software on the root directory of a PC hard drive. (b) To format a disk, enter the text that follows on your PC: > FMCPREP<DRIVE>:<Airline ID where: <drive> is the letter "A" or "B" of the PCs 3.5 inch disk drive. Airline ID> is the name of the airline maintenance site (11 characters maximum). example: FMCPREP B: Cincinatti SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-009 (2) Make sure the MAINT BITE INDEX 1/1 page shows on the CDU. (a) If the MAINT BITE INDEX 1/1 page is not shown, do these steps: 1) Push the INIT REF key. 2) Push the LSK adjacent to MAINT> to show the MAINT BITE INDEX 1/1 page. SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-010 (3) Push the LSK adjacent to FMC DOWNLOAD>. SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-023 (4) Follow the directions on the FMC DATA LOADER page. (a) Select Capt Left System or F/O Right System on Data Load Select switch. (b) Select FMC on the Data Load System Select switch. (c) Select FMC Source on the Overhead Source Select Panel. NOTE: When the FMC Source Select Switch is in the Both On Right Position the diagnostic data from the F/Os or Right FMC will be downloaded. 34-61-00 SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-012 (5) Push the LSK adjacent to CONTINUE. NOTE: If you push the LSK adjacent to PRESS HERE TO EXIT>, the FMC will do a cold start power-up. SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-028 (6) Remove the media from the drive or port when the download is complete. SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-013 (7) Put the formatted disk into the data loader disk drive. NOTE: If the disk is write protected, the FMC download will not continue from this page. Remove the disk and set the write- protected tab to the write position. Put the disk back into the data loader disk drive. NOTE: The disk may only contain FMC download data. SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-014 (8) The FMC automatically starts the data transfer sequence. NOTE: When the data transfer is complete, the FMC DATA LOADER page shows DOWNLOAD COMPLETE. SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-015 (9) Remove the disk and push the LSK adjacent to PRESS HERE TO EXIT>. NOTE: If you push the LSK adjacent to PRESS HERE TO EXIT>, the FMC will do a cold start power-up. 056-063, 067-078, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 081 POST SB 737-34-2000 SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-021 (10) To download data from the second FMC, set the FMC Source Select Switch position to the other FMC and do the Diagnostic Data Transfer task again. NOTE: A single diskette or USB flash drive has sufficient capacity to hold data from both FMCs. ALL SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-022 (11) After you make a copy of the data on the disk or USB flash drive, send the disk or data to the vendor. NOTE: For the USB flash drive, use the eADL Connect software to extract the data.

D. Data Transfer Failure Indications

SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-017 (1) If the disk that you put into the data loader disk drive contains an FMC operational program or database, the FMC DATA LOADER page shows this message: WARNING: DISK UNUSABLE OFP OR DB DISK INSERTED (a) Replace the disk with a correctly formatted disk. 34-61-00 SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-018 (2) If the disk that you put into the data loader disk drive is not write-protected and contains data (may be FMC diagnostic transfer data from the currently selected FMC) that is not an FMC operational program or database, the FMC DATA LOADER page shows this message: WARNING: DISK UNUSABLE DISK CONTAINS DATA (a) Remove the disk from the data loader disk drive. (b) Push the LSK adjacent to PRESS HERE TO RETRY>. SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-019 (3) If the disk that you put into the data loader disk drive is not write-protected and is not formatted by the FMCPREP software, the FMC DATA LOADER page shows this message: WARNING: DISK UNUSABLE FORMAT DISK USING THE FMCPREP PC UTILITY (a) Remove the disk from the data loader disk drive. (b) Push the LSK adjacent to PRESS HERE TO RETRY>. SUBTASK 34-61-00-750-020 (4) If the diagnostic data transfer is not successful for any other reason, the FMC DATALOADER page shows this message: DEVICE NOT PRESENT DISK WAS REMOVED OR INTERFACE HAS FAILED (a) Push the LSK adjacent to PRESS HERE TO RETRY>.

34-61-00-730-801Flight Management Computer System - System TestPDF p. 1175

3. Flight Management Computer System - System Test

A. General

(1) The system test does a complete check of the Flight Management Computer System (FMCS). The test makes sure that the system operates correctly. (2) You can do the tests in sequence or one at a time. All tests must be done to make sure that the system operates correctly. The Prepare For Test steps must be done before each test or sequence of tests.

B. References

Reference Title 06-41-00-800-801 Finding an Access Door or Panel on the Lower Half of the Fuselage (P/B 201) 32-00-01-480-801 Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation (P/B 201) 34-61-00

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

Number Name/Location 192CL ECS Access Door 192CR ECS Access Door 192DR ECS High Pressure Access Door

34-61-00-800-801FMCS Performance Factors - AdjustmentPDF p. 1191

4. FMCS Performance Factors - Adjustment

A. General

(1) This task gives steps to adjust these performance factors: (a) Drag factor (b) F-F factor 34-61-00 (c) Maneuver margin (d) Minimum cruise time (e) Minimum rate of climb (climb) margin (f) Minimum rate of climb (cruise) margin (g) Minimum rate of climb (engine out) margin. (2) You can do these adjustments in sequence or one at a time. The Prepare For Adjustment steps must be done before each adjustment or sequence of adjustments. NOTE: If a factor has had its entry capability disabled by a loadable performance defaults database, you cannot change its value using this procedure. You must load a new performance defaults database with the new factor value. (3) The Control Display Unit (CDU) is necessary for this procedure. You can use CDU No. 1 or CDU No. 2 to do this procedure.

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

3. FMCS CDU Display Cleaning

A. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B50012 Cleaner - Optical Cleaning, Calotherm Solution - Supaspray B50013 Cloth - Calocoat Hi-T ech Lenscloth - Supacloth G02457 Cleaner - Wet/Dry Anti-Static Sachet - ALGLAS Visial ALG/CR 215

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 210 Subzone - Control Compartment - Body Station 178.00 to Body Station 259.50

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 34-61-01-100-002 (1) Clean the display surface of the FMCS control display unit (CDU) with the Supaspray cleaner, B50012, and the Supacloth cloth, B50013, or the ALGLAS Visial cleaner, G02457: (a) Apply 2 or 3 sprays of the Supaspray to the Supacloth, or open the wet sachet. (b) Use the moist cloth or the wet sachet to clean the display surface in a straight line from top to bottom. (c) Gradually move from one side of the display surface to the other side while you clean from top to bottom. (d) When the display surface is clean, use a clean, dry area of the cloth or the dry sachet in a straight line from top to bottom to dry the display surface.

G. FMCS Transfer Relay Installation Test

SUBTASK 34-61-04-710-001 (1) Do these steps for the annunciator test: (a) Make sure the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH is set to the NORMAL position. NOTE: If the MENU page is displayed on either CDU, press the LSK adjacent to FMC on that CDU. (b) Push the CLR Key on the CDUs to remove the alert level message from the CDU scratchpad. (c) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name A 6 C01017 FMCS CMPTR 1 (d) Make sure the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's (P1) and first officer's (P3) instrument panels come on. (e) Push the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the autoflight status annunciators (ASAs) and make sure that the lights go off. (f) Set the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH to the BOTH ON R position. NOTE: If the MENU page is displayed on either CDU, press the LSK adjacent to FMC on that CDU. (g) Push the CLR Key on the CDUs to remove the alert level message from the CDU scratchpad. (h) Make sure that the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's and first officer's ASAs are off. (i) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 16 C01262 FMCS CMPTR 2 34-61-04 (j) Make sure the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's and first officer's ASAs come on. (k) Push the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the ASAs and make sure that the lights go off. (l) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name A 6 C01017 FMCS CMPTR 1 (m) After 15 seconds, set the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH to the BOTH ON L position. NOTE: If the MENU page is displayed on either CDU, press the LSK adjacent to FMC on that CDU. (n) Push the CLR Key on the CDUs to remove the alert level message from the CDU scratchpad. (o) Make sure that the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's and first officer's ASAs are off. (p) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 16 C01262 FMCS CMPTR 2 (q) After 15 seconds, set the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH to the NORMAL position. (r) Make sure that the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's and first officer's ASAs are still off. (s) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name A 6 C01017 FMCS CMPTR 1 (t) Put the MASTER DIM and TEST switch in the TEST position. (u) Make sure that the MSG, CALL, FAIL, OFST , and EXEC annunciator lights on the CDUs come on. (v) Make sure that the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the captain's and first officer's ASAs come on. (w) Push the FMC P/RST annunciator lights on the ASAs and make sure that the lights go off. (x) Put the MASTER DIM and TEST switch in the DIM position. (y) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name A 6 C01017 FMCS CMPTR 1

H. Operational Program, Navigation Database, and Fixed Outputs Checks

SUBTASK 34-61-04-710-002 (1) If it is necessary, do the “Prepare for Test” steps from Flight Management Computer System - Operational Test, TASK 34-61-00-710-801. 34-61-04 SUBTASK 34-61-04-710-003 (2) Do these steps to examine the operational program and navigation database: (a) Set the FMC SOURCE SELECT SWITCH to the BOTH ON L position. (b) Push the INIT REF key on the two CDUs. (c) Push the line select key (LSK) adjacent to INDEX on the two CDUs. (d) Push the LSK adjacent to IDENTon the two CDUs. (e) Make sure the two CDUs show the IDENT 1/X page. (f) Make sure the part number of the OP PROGRAM is correct on the two CDUs.
